question.en:
"The idea that space and time form a four-dimensional continuum was first suggested by Hermann Minkowski as a natural consequence of Einstein's Special Theory of Relativity. In this framework, time is not an independent, absolute entity, as Newton had assumed, but rather interwoven with the three spatial dimensions into a single fabric known as space-time. Events occur at points in this space-time, and their separation is governed not by traditional Euclidean distance but by the relativistic interval, which remains invariant under changes of reference frame. This deep connection between space and time implies that the passage of time is not universal but relative: what one observer perceives as simultaneous may differ for another observer in relative motion. This concept becomes even more profound when we introduce gravity, as formulated in Einstein’s General Theory of Relativity. Gravity is no longer thought of as a force in the Newtonian sense but rather as the curvature of space-time caused by the presence of mass and energy. Objects moving within this curved space-time follow geodesics—the natural paths dictated by the warping of space and time itself. This leads to the astonishing prediction that time runs differently in regions of varying gravitational potential: near a massive body, such as a black hole, time slows relative to an observer in free space. This effect, known as gravitational time dilation, has been confirmed through precise experiments, such as the observation that clocks aboard satellites tick slightly faster than those on Earth's surface due to weaker gravity."

question.en:
Read the passage and answer the questions: "Normal science, the activity in which most scientists inevitably spend almost all their time, is based on the assumption that the scientific community knows what the world is like. Scientists take great pains to defend that assumption, often restricting their vision to the phenomena that the existing paradigm has defined as relevant. When research proceeds in this fashion, findings tend to be incremental, reinforcing the established framework rather than challenging it. Yet, over time, anomalies-empirical observations that cannot be explained within the current paradigm-accumulate. Initially, these anomalies are dismissed as errors or as problems to be solved within the existing theoretical structure. However, as these anomalies grow in number and significance, they begin to erode confidence in the prevailing paradigm. The resolution of such crises is not a straightforward process of falsification, as Popper might suggest, but rather a transformation in the very way scientists see the world. Scientific revolutions occur when a new paradigm emerges-one that is not merely an extension of the old but a fundamental reconceptualization of reality. This shift is not purely logical or empirical; it involves a radical change in perspective, akin to a gestalt switch. The Copernican Revolution, for example, did not merely adjust astronomical calculations; it redefined the very framework through which celestial motion was understood. Similarly, Einstein's theory of relativity did not just modify Newtonian mechanics but replaced its foundational assumptions about space and time.

question.en:
Read the passage and answer the questions: The argument of this book is that we, and all other animals, are machines created by our genes. Like successful Chicago gangsters, our genes have survived sometimes for millions of years in a highly competitive world. This has entailed ruthless selfishness in gene selection, yet paradoxically it has also favored behaviors that, at an organismal level, may appear cooperative or even altruistic. The key to understanding this paradox lies in recognizing that what matters is not the survival of the individual organism, nor even the species, but rather the continuity of the genes themselves. Natural selection, therefore, operates at the level of replicators-genes-rather than the individual creatures they construct as temporary vehicles. These survival machines, whether they be humans, ants, or oak trees, serve merely as the means through which genes propagate. This gene-centered view of evolution helps explain many otherwise puzzling phenomena in nature. For example, kin selection provides a compelling reason why apparent acts of altruism, such as worker ants sacrificing their ability to reproduce, can evolve: by ensuring the survival and reproduction of closely related individuals, an organism still promotes the continuity of its genetic lineage. This perspective challenges the common anthropocentric tendency to view evolution as a process geared toward the 'good of the species. In reality, natural selection cares nothing for abstract collective welfare; it blindly favors gene variants that are better at replicating, regardless of their consequences beyond that singular goal.

question.en:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. My younger brother **will teaches** english language to the graduate students.





[CPO, 11 Dec 2025, Shift 1]

solution.en:
**Explanation:**

The underlined segment **'will teaches'** is incorrect because **'will' is a modal auxiliary verb**, and a modal verb must always be followed by the **base form (V1)** of the main verb.

Therefore, **'will teaches' ❌** should be changed to **'will teach' ✅**.

**Why not 'can teach'?**
'Can teach' is grammatically correct, but it changes the meaning of the sentence. **'Can' expresses ability or possibility**, whereas **'will' expresses a future action or intention**.

• **He will teach English.** → He is going to teach English in the future.
• **He can teach English.** → He has the ability to teach English.

Since the original sentence uses **'will'** and the question asks for the most appropriate substitution without changing the intended meaning, **'will teach'** is the correct answer.

**Important Rule:** After modal verbs such as **will, can, could, may, might, shall, should, must**, the **base form (V1)** of the verb is used.

Examples:
• He **will teach** English. ✅
• He **can teach** English. ✅
• She **will go** there. ✅
• They **can solve** the problem. ✅

Thus, **'will teaches' → 'will teach'**.

**Correct Answer: will teach**

question.en:
Read the passage and answer the questions: Habits, scientists say, emerge because the brain is constantly looking for ways to save effort. Left to its own devices, the brain will try to make almost any routine into a habit, because habits allow our minds to ramp down more often. This effort-saving instinct is a huge advantage. An efficient brain requires less room, which makes for a smaller head, which makes childbirth easier, and therefore makes survival more likely. But conserving mental effort is only part of the story. Habits also have a powerful impact on our behaviors because once they are formed, they operate automatically. Even more importantly, habits can be changed, replaced, or ignored-but only if we understand how they work. At the core of every habit is a neurological loop that consists of three parts: a cue, a routine, and a reward. This loop is the foundation of all habitual behaviors. The cue is the trigger that tells your brain to go into automatic mode, the routine is the behavior itself, and the reward is what helps your brain remember the loop in the future. Understanding this loop is the first step in taking control of habits, whether you want to break a bad habit or create a new one.

question.en:
Read the passage and answer the questions: "The truth of the self-conscious individual lies not in its immediate certainty, but in the dialectical movement of its becoming. Consciousness, in its pursuit of knowledge, initially assumes that its object is something external and independent. Yet, through the labor of experience, it discovers that this object is not truly separate but is mediated by consciousness itself. The apparent duality of subject and object is thus sublated in the dialectic, revealing that knowledge is not the passive reception of an external truth but an active process in which consciousness shapes and transforms its own reality. This movement unfolds through a series of contradictions, in which each stage of consciousness, believing itself to have attained certainty, encounters its own inadequacy. The master-slave dialectic exemplifies this: self-consciousness seeks recognition from another, yet in asserting its dominance over the other, it paradoxically undermines its own freedom. The master, in reducing the slave to a mere instrument, deprives himself of a fully realized recognition. Meanwhile, the slave, through labor and self-transformation, attains a deeper awareness of autonomy, demonstrating that freedom is not given but achieved through negation and overcoming.

**Ans: as well as**

question.en:
Read the passage and answer the questions: "The explanation of a work is always sought in the man or woman who produced it, as if it were always, in the end, through the voice of a single person that literature spoke: through the voice of a single person and the imprints of his or her passions. The image of literature that we seek to sustain is tyrannically centered on the author, his life, his history, and his intentions. But to give a text an Author is to impose a limit on that text, to furnish it with a final signified, to close the writing. Such a conception is born of the rationalist and capitalist ideologies that have placed the individual at the center of history, emphasizing his authority and coherence. Yet, in reality, writing is a destruction of every voice, of every point of origin. Writing begins at the moment the Author is set aside, and language speaks-not the Author. To refuse the Author is not to refuse meaning, but to refuse the tyranny of a single, authoritative meaning. The text, instead, becomes a space of multiple interpretations, where meaning is neither fixed nor final. The unity of a text is not located in its origin but in its destination; it is the reader, not the Author, who gives meaning to a text. This radical displacement shifts the power from the creator to the interpreter, from the supposed intention of the writer to the infinite play of signifiers within the text itself.

question.en:
"The idea that space and time form a four-dimensional continuum was first suggested by Hermann Minkowski as a natural consequence of Einstein's Special Theory of Relativity. In this framework, time is not an independent, absolute entity, as Newton had assumed, but rather interwoven with the three spatial dimensions into a single fabric known as space-time. Events occur at points in this space-time, and their separation is governed not by traditional Euclidean distance but by the relativistic interval, which remains invariant under changes of reference frame. This deep connection between space and time implies that the passage of time is not universal but relative: what one observer perceives as simultaneous may differ for another observer in relative motion. This concept becomes even more profound when we introduce gravity, as formulated in Einstein’s General Theory of Relativity. Gravity is no longer thought of as a force in the Newtonian sense but rather as the curvature of space-time caused by the presence of mass and energy. Objects moving within this curved space-time follow geodesics—the natural paths dictated by the warping of space and time itself. This leads to the astonishing prediction that time runs differently in regions of varying gravitational potential: near a massive body, such as a black hole, time slows relative to an observer in free space. This effect, known as gravitational time dilation, has been confirmed through precise experiments, such as the observation that clocks aboard satellites tick slightly faster than those on Earth's surface due to weaker gravity."

question.en:
Read the passage and answer the questions: "Normal science, the activity in which most scientists inevitably spend almost all their time, is based on the assumption that the scientific community knows what the world is like. Scientists take great pains to defend that assumption, often restricting their vision to the phenomena that the existing paradigm has defined as relevant. When research proceeds in this fashion, findings tend to be incremental, reinforcing the established framework rather than challenging it. Yet, over time, anomalies-empirical observations that cannot be explained within the current paradigm-accumulate. Initially, these anomalies are dismissed as errors or as problems to be solved within the existing theoretical structure. However, as these anomalies grow in number and significance, they begin to erode confidence in the prevailing paradigm. The resolution of such crises is not a straightforward process of falsification, as Popper might suggest, but rather a transformation in the very way scientists see the world. Scientific revolutions occur when a new paradigm emerges-one that is not merely an extension of the old but a fundamental reconceptualization of reality. This shift is not purely logical or empirical; it involves a radical change in perspective, akin to a gestalt switch. The Copernican Revolution, for example, did not merely adjust astronomical calculations; it redefined the very framework through which celestial motion was understood. Similarly, Einstein's theory of relativity did not just modify Newtonian mechanics but replaced its foundational assumptions about space and time.

question.en:
Read the passage and answer the questions: The argument of this book is that we, and all other animals, are machines created by our genes. Like successful Chicago gangsters, our genes have survived sometimes for millions of years in a highly competitive world. This has entailed ruthless selfishness in gene selection, yet paradoxically it has also favored behaviors that, at an organismal level, may appear cooperative or even altruistic. The key to understanding this paradox lies in recognizing that what matters is not the survival of the individual organism, nor even the species, but rather the continuity of the genes themselves. Natural selection, therefore, operates at the level of replicators-genes-rather than the individual creatures they construct as temporary vehicles. These survival machines, whether they be humans, ants, or oak trees, serve merely as the means through which genes propagate. This gene-centered view of evolution helps explain many otherwise puzzling phenomena in nature. For example, kin selection provides a compelling reason why apparent acts of altruism, such as worker ants sacrificing their ability to reproduce, can evolve: by ensuring the survival and reproduction of closely related individuals, an organism still promotes the continuity of its genetic lineage. This perspective challenges the common anthropocentric tendency to view evolution as a process geared toward the 'good of the species. In reality, natural selection cares nothing for abstract collective welfare; it blindly favors gene variants that are better at replicating, regardless of their consequences beyond that singular goal.

question.en:
Given below are four jumbled parts of a sentence. Select the option that gives their correct order.
A) has been attributed by many climate scientists
B) the unprecedented frequency of extreme weather events
C) to the steady rise in global atmospheric temperatures
D) observed across various continents over the last decade
[CGL Tier-2]

solution.en:
The sentence begins naturally with the subject phrase “the unprecedented frequency of extreme weather events,” followed by “observed across various continents over the last decade,” then the verb phrase “has been attributed by many climate scientists,” and finally the cause “to the steady rise in global atmospheric temperatures.” So the correct order is B-D-A-C.
Learning points:
- Find the subject first
- Place modifiers next to the noun they describe
- Verb phrase should follow the subject
- Cause/explanation phrases often come at the end

question.en:
Given below are four jumbled parts of a sentence. Select the option that gives their correct order.
A) by the intricate tapestry of
B) the philosopher was captivated
C) that define human existence
D) moral and ethical dilemmas
[CGL Tier-2]

solution.en:
The proper sentence is: “The philosopher was captivated by the intricate tapestry of moral and ethical dilemmas that define human existence.” This follows the order B-A-D-C. It starts with the subject and verb, then the prepositional phrase, then the object, and finally the relative clause.
Learning points:
- Relative clause “that define...” should follow the noun it modifies
- “Captivated by” is a fixed expression
- Start with subject + verb for clarity

question.en:
Given below are four jumbled parts of a sentence. Select the option that gives their correct order.
A) has been attributed by many climate scientists
B) the unprecedented frequency of extreme weather events
C) to the steady rise in global atmospheric temperatures
D) observed across various continents over the last decade
[CGL Tier-2]

solution.en:
The sentence begins naturally with the subject phrase “the unprecedented frequency of extreme weather events,” followed by “observed across various continents over the last decade,” then the verb phrase “has been attributed by many climate scientists,” and finally the cause “to the steady rise in global atmospheric temperatures.” So the correct order is B-D-A-C.
Learning points:
- Find the subject first
- Place modifiers next to the noun they describe
- Verb phrase should follow the subject
- Cause/explanation phrases often come at the end

A) by the intricate tapestry of
B) the philosopher was captivated
C) that define human existence
D) moral and ethical dilemmas
[CGL Tier-2]

solution.en:
The proper sentence is: “The philosopher was captivated by the intricate tapestry of moral and ethical dilemmas that define human existence.” This follows the order B-A-D-C. It starts with the subject and verb, then the prepositional phrase, then the object, and finally the relative clause.
Learning points:
- Relative clause “that define...” should follow the noun it modifies
- “Captivated by” is a fixed expression
- Start with subject + verb for clarity

question.en:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order.
A. Faced with the high cost and scarcity of Indian indigo, European manufacturers were forced to rely on the woad plant for their dyeing needs.
B. However, cloth dyers still preferred indigo, as it produced a significantly richer and more vibrant blue than woad ever could.
C. Since woad thrived in temperate climates, it was readily available and easily cultivated throughout Europe.
D. Indian indigo was prohibitively expensive, and only meager quantities ever reached European markets.
[CGL Tier-2]

solution.en:
The best flow starts with D, which introduces the problem of scarce and expensive Indian indigo. Then A explains the consequence: manufacturers relied on woad. C gives the reason why woad was used—it was available in Europe. B ends with contrast using “However,” showing that indigo was still preferred. So the correct order is D-A-C-B.
Learning points:
- Transitional words like “However” often appear later
- Cause should follow context
- Build order: problem → reaction → reason → contrast

question.en:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order.
A. Here, the picture-perfect French Quarter and heritage-laden Tamil streets blend into one another.
B. Across many metropolitan cities, there exists a visible conflict in how the old and the new coexist.
C. The old and new, like two different worlds, surviving side by side yet never crossing that chasm.
D. However, Puducherry stands as a striking exception, where these very contrasts are celebrated rather than endured.
[CGL Tier-2]

solution.en:
B sets up the general idea of conflict in cities. D introduces Puducherry as an exception. A explains how that exception appears there. C concludes by describing the usual contrast more poetically in relation to the larger idea. Thus B-D-A-C is the best arrangement.
Learning points:
- “However” usually introduces contrast after a general statement
- “Here” in A refers to Puducherry introduced in D
- Pronoun/reference clues help in jumbled sentences

Q: After that, she turned the fragile pages carefully so as not to break them any more.
R: With a long history filled with tales, the book has been handed down through the centuries.
S: Before starting the restoration procedure, she got the equipment and supplies she would need ready.
[SSC CHSL Tier 1, 15 Nov 2025, Shift-3]
[CHSL, 15 Nov 2025, Shift 3]

solution.en: Sentence R introduces the subject, the historical book. Sentence S initiates the chronological process by stating her preparatory steps before restoration. Sentence P describes her first active step (examining), and Q follows sequentially (**After that**).

question.en:
Rearrange the following sentences to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:
P. He spent his days in the lab, carefully scanning samples under a microscope.
Q. Dr. Alistair Finch was an accomplished biologist who specialized in the discovery of new species.
R. His peers would tease him that he looked more upon the microbial world than on the actual one.
S. His greatest find was from a small, ordinary pond deep in the Amazon rainforest.
[CHSL, 17 Nov 2025, Shift 1]

solution.en: The logical sequence is: First, introduce Dr. Finch (Q), then describe his daily work in the lab (P), followed by his peers' teasing about his dedication to the microbial world (R), and finally his greatest discovery (S). QPRS forms a coherent paragraph that moves from introduction → daily routine → peers' reaction → achievement.

question.en:
Rearrange the following sentence parts to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:
P. She repeatedly listened to the song, taking in its passion and rhythm.
Q. She made a sequence of motions and connected them to form a smooth flow.
R. Her artistic vision was brought to the stage by the dancers, who executed the work brilliantly.
S. She taught the dance to her troupe, refining each step and making sure every moment was synchronized.
[CHSL, 17 Nov 2025, Shift 1]

solution.en: The logical sequence is: First, she listens to the song for inspiration (P), then she creates a sequence of dance motions (Q), next she teaches the dance to her troupe (S), and finally the dancers bring her vision to the stage (R). PQSR follows the natural creative process: inspiration → creation → teaching → performance.

question.en:
Rearrange the following sentences to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:
P. He disassembled the old engine with care, marking each component precisely.
Q. He torqued the bolts to the precise specifications, put in new gaskets, and replaced old parts.
R. After reassembling the engine, he put it back in the vehicle and reattached all of the hoses.
S. On the first turn of the key, the engine flickered to life and resumed its flawless operation.
[CHSL, 17 Nov 2025, Shift 2]

solution.en: First the engine is disassembled, then repaired and parts replaced, then reassembled and put back, and finally it starts. So the correct sequence is P, Q, R, S.

question.en:
Rearrange the following sentences to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:
P: As a result, the software significantly improved operational efficiency across departments.
Q: The team worked tirelessly, refining the code and testing each feature for compatibility.
R: It was designed to simplify daily tasks and provide real-time data analysis.
S: A groundbreaking new software was developed to streamline workflow and increase productivity.
[CHSL, 17 Nov 2025, Shift 2]

solution.en: The paragraph logically begins with the introduction of the software, then its purpose, then the team's work on it, and finally the result. Hence S, R, Q, P.

question.en:
Rearrange the following sentence parts to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:
P. She poured the hot liquid into her favourite mug.
Q. A downpour had started raining hard, beating against the windowpanes in steady rhythm.
R. The kitchen was filled with the scent of cinnamon and cloves, a comforting and warm smell.
S. It was a fantastic night to have a mug of hot cider.
[CHSL, 17 Nov 2025, Shift 3]

solution.en: First comes the rainy setting (Q), then the general conclusion (S), then the action of pouring cider (R and P fit as description and action). The best coherent sequence is **QSRP**.

question.en:
Rearrange the following sentence parts to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:
P. The air was heavy with the reek of seaweed and salt.
Q. He walked down the deserted beach, the sand cool against his bare feet.
R. The sun went below the horizon, coloring the sky with orange, pink, and purple colors.
S. The waves gently lapped at the shore, a constant, soothing sound.
[CHSL, 17 Nov 2025, Shift 3]

solution.en: The paragraph begins with the man walking on the beach (Q), then describes the smell (P), the sound (S), and finally the sunset scene (R).

question.en:
Rearrange the following sentence parts to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:
P. He took a very thin slice of a tissue sample and placed it on a glass slide.
Q. He added a single drop of a staining solution to make the cells visible.
R. He carefully placed a thin cover slip over the sample to protect it.
S. He placed the slide under the microscope to begin his examination.
[CHSL, 21 Nov 2025, Shift 2]

solution.en: The correct sequence follows the proper process of preparing a microscope slide. First, the tissue sample is placed on the slide (P), then stain is added (Q), after that the cover slip is placed (R), and finally the slide is observed under the microscope (S). The other sequences disturb the natural scientific order.

question.en:
Rearrange the following sentences to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:
P. A robot built to tackle a challenging challenge served as the students' final assignment.
Q. The code that would enable the machine to traverse a maze was written over weeks.
R. Their engineering, programming, and design abilities came together to create it.
S. The robot's faultless performance demonstrated their commitment and cooperation.
[CHSL, 21 Nov 2025, Shift 2]

solution.en: The paragraph should begin with the introduction of the robot as the final assignment (P). Then it explains how the students' skills came together to create it (R), followed by the coding work done over weeks (Q). Finally, the successful performance is mentioned as the result (S). This gives a logical beginning, development, and conclusion.

question.en:
**Rearrange the following sentences to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:**

P. He fuelled his body for the rigorous workout by adhering to a particular diet and drinking plenty of water.
Q. He pushed his body to its limits by going on lengthy runs on the weekends.
R. Throughout the week, he increased his endurance by running shorter distances.
S. He was tired but elated when he crossed the finish line on race day.
[CHSL, 21 Nov 2025, Shift 3]

solution.en: This question tests paragraph coherence and logical sequence. The correct order is P, R, Q, S. The logical flow is: P (preparation through diet) → R (building endurance during weekdays) → Q (pushing limits on weekends) → S (final race day result). This creates a chronological progression from preparation to training to the final race. Option (b) follows this natural sequence of events in a training story.

question.en:
**Rearrange the following sentences to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:**

P: The public park in the city was converted into a lively community centre with green areas and recreational facilities.
Q: It was a much-awaited project that united the community and had a friendly environment.
R: The park soon became a favourite destination for families, fitness buffs, and nature enthusiasts.
S: Volunteers and local businesses joined hands to donate resources such as plants, benches, and tools.
[CHSL, 21 Nov 2025, Shift 3]

solution.en: This question tests logical sequencing of events in a paragraph. The correct order is P, S, Q, R. The logical flow is: P (park conversion announcement) → S (community contribution) → Q (project impact on community) → R (final result as popular destination). This creates a coherent narrative from the initial conversion through community involvement to the final outcome. Option (a) presents this natural progression of the park development story.

question.en:
Rearrange the following sentence parts to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:
P. In search of the queen bee, he cautiously opened the beehive and examined the frames.
Q. He took out a honey frame and scraped off the wax covers with a knife.
R. He put the frame in an extractor, which used centrifugal force to spin the honey out.
S. As a delightful reward for his labour, he filled jars with the delicious, fresh honey.
[CHSL, 22 Nov 2025, Shift 1]

solution.en: The logical sequence is opening and examining the hive, taking out the frame, extracting the honey, and finally filling jars.

question.en:
Rearrange the following sentences to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:
P. He turned the board towards the coast when he noticed a nice swell coming.
Q. In search of the ideal wave, he paddled his board out to the deep water.
R. He pushed up onto his feet after paddling hard, cautiously balancing on the board.
S. He rode the wave to the sand for a few beautiful seconds.
[CHSL, 22 Nov 2025, Shift 1]

solution.en: First he paddles out, then notices the swell and turns, then stands up, and finally rides the wave.

question.en:
Rearrange the following sentence parts to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:
P. He started leaning big branches on a solid wood after discovering a natural hollow in the ground.
Q. He made a frame for the walls by weaving smaller branches between the major supports.
R. To provide insulation, he covered the structure with thick grass and leaf layers.
S. He was shielded from the rain and wind within the completed shelter.
[CHSL, 22 Nov 2025, Shift 2]

solution.en: First the shelter structure begins with supports, then a wall frame is made, then insulation is added, and finally the completed shelter provides protection.

question.en:
Rearrange the following sentences to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:
P. A wonder of contemporary urban planning was the city's new public transport system.
Q. It was intended to lessen traffic jams and enhance the city's air quality overall.
R. The project needed a significant government investment and took more than ten years to finish.
S. The system was a massive hit with commuters, even if it was expensive.
[CHSL, 22 Nov 2025, Shift 2]

solution.en: The paragraph should first introduce the transport system, then mention its purpose, then its development details, and finally its public success.

question.en:
Rearrange the following sentence parts to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:
P. He worked hard every day to improve his skills.
Q. As a result, he became one of the best players on the team.
R. At first, he was not very good at football.
S. However, he never gave up and kept practicing.
[CHSL, 26 Nov 2025, Shift 1]

solution.en: The correct order is R,S,P,Q because this sequence forms a meaningful and grammatically coherent arrangement. Therefore, option (c) is the correct answer.

question.en:
Rearrange the following sentence parts to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:
P. He crafted his thoughts into a careful message, his fingers flying across the keys.
Q. He swiftly entered a lengthy string of characters and numbers that was the recipient's email address.
R. A simple subject line summarizes the entire point of the message.
S. He breathed a last sigh of relief as he hit the send button and saw the email disappear.
[CHSL, 26 Nov 2025, Shift 1]

solution.en: First, the recipient’s email address is entered (Q), then the subject line is given (R), next the message is composed (P), and finally the send button is pressed (S). Thus the correct order is **Q,R,P,S**.

question.en:
Rearrange the following sentences to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:
P. She gracefully finished with her arms up after landing flawlessly on both feet.
Q. She flipped and twisted her body in midair as she blasted herself off the springboard.
R. She ran briskly in the direction of the vault to start her routine.
S. With a faultless performance and a perfect score, she bowed to the judges and the audience.
[CHSL, 26 Nov 2025, Shift 1]

solution.en: The gymnast first starts her run (R), then performs the aerial movement (Q), then lands and finishes (P), and finally bows after the performance (S). So the correct order is **R,Q,P,S**.

question.en:
Rearrange the following sentence parts to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:
P. She presented the findings to her team, revealing new patterns in the business.
Q. She created a series of functions to clean and transform the data, making it usable.
R. She developed a dashboard to visualise the insights and trends hidden in the data.
S. She wrote a script to extract raw data from multiple sources.
[CHSL, 26 Nov 2025, Shift 2]

solution.en: The logical sequence is: first raw data is extracted (S), then it is cleaned and transformed (Q), then visualised in a dashboard (R), and finally the findings are presented (P).

question.en:
Rearrange the following sentences to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:
P. The group of scientists was looking for a new planet outside of our solar system, known as an exoplanet.
Q. They observed the far-off star using a powerful telescope in search of a telltale dimming of its brightness.
R. They found a new planet, establishing its existence through a series of follow-up observations.
S. This slight dimming would indicate a planet passing in front of the star.
[CHSL, 26 Nov 2025, Shift 2]

solution.en: First, the aim is introduced (P). Then the observation method is described (Q). Next, the meaning of the dimming is explained (S). Finally, the discovery is confirmed (R).

question.en:
Rearrange the following sentence parts to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:
P. He heated a bar of steel in the forge until it glowed a bright, brilliant orange.
Q. He hammered the hot metal on the anvil, shaping it into the form he desired.
R. He tempered the finished piece, dipping it in oil to give it strength and durability.
S. The forged object was a strong, beautiful piece, born of fire and brute force.
[CHSL, 26 Nov 2025, Shift 3]

solution.en: The logical sequence of forging is: heating the metal (P), hammering it into shape (Q), describing the forged object (S), and then tempering the finished piece (R), as given in the source sequence.

question.en:
Rearrange the following sentence parts to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:
P. He removed all old paint and flaws from the whole automobile body by sanding it.
Q. He watched the fresh paint dry to a smooth finish after applying multiple thin, even coats.
R. He shielded the windows and trim from overspray by carefully masking them off.
S. The vehicle had a perfect colour, appeared brand new, and was prepared for driving.
[CHSL, 27 Nov 2025, Shift 1]

solution.en: First, the surface must be prepared by sanding (**P**). Then nearby parts are protected by masking (**R**). After that, paint is applied and allowed to dry (**Q**). Finally, the result is described (**S**). So the correct order is **P, R, Q, S**.

question.en:
Rearrange the following sentence parts to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:
P. He collected water from a stream into a pot and placed it over a fire.
Q. He brought the water to a rolling boil for several minutes, killing all the pathogens.
R. He took a drink of the clear, safe water, his thirst finally quenched.
S. He allowed the water to cool, then poured it through a cloth to filter out any sediment.
[CHSL, 27 Nov 2025, Shift 2]

solution.en: First he collects and heats the water (P), then boils it (Q), then cools and filters it (S), and finally drinks it (R). This is the only logical sequence.

question.en:
Rearrange the following sentences to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:
P. As a result, they were able to produce crops that would feed a population that was growing quickly.
Q. The Incas were skilled builders who carved terraces onto the Andes mountains' precipitous slopes.
R. Where there had previously been no level, fruitful soil, these terraces produced it.
S. Their empire's stability and wealth were mainly due to their agricultural inventiveness.
[CHSL, 27 Nov 2025, Shift 2]

solution.en: The paragraph should begin with the subject, the Incas (Q). Then it explains the effect of terraces (R), then the result on food production (P), and ends with the broad conclusion about their empire (S).

question.en:
Rearrange the following sentences to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:
P. Its expansive plains and rich soil, perfect for farming and grazing, drew them in.
Q. A surge of settlers started to go west over the American continent in the 19th century.
R. Their difficult voyage was motivated by the prospect of a fresh life and inexpensive land.
S. This large-scale migration permanently altered the region's culture and geography.
[CHSL, 27 Nov 2025, Shift 3]

solution.en: Q introduces the topic, R explains the motivation of the settlers, P adds what attracted them, and S concludes with the impact. So the correct order is Q-R-P-S.

question.en:
Rearrange the following sentence parts to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:
P. He created mockups of each screen the user would view in order to build the user interface.
Q. He programmed the app's features and response, writing the fundamental logic.
R. He fixed errors and made sure the app ran well by testing it on a variety of devices.
S. He made the finished product available for download by uploading it to the app store.
[CHSL, 28 Nov 2025, Shift 2]

solution.en: The logical order of app development is: first design the interface (P), then program the features (Q), then test and fix errors (R), and finally upload the finished app (S).

question.en:
Rearrange the following sentences to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:
P. A robot built to tackle a challenging challenge served as the students' final assignment.
Q. The code that would enable the machine to traverse a maze was written over the course of weeks.
R. Their engineering, programming, and design abilities came together to create it.
S. Their commitment and cooperation were demonstrated by the robot's faultless performance.
[CHSL, 28 Nov 2025, Shift 2]

solution.en: The paragraph should begin with the assignment itself (P), then describe the combined skills used (R), then the coding process (Q), and finally the successful outcome (S).

question.en:
Rearrange the following sentence parts to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:
P. He connected the modem to the wall and the wireless router to the modem.
Q. He followed the setup wizard on his computer, configuring the network's name and password.
R. He connected all his devices to the new network, from his phone to his smart TV.
S. He performed a speed test, confirming his home now had a strong and reliable connection.
[CHSL, 29 Nov 2025, Shift 2]

solution.en: First the physical setup is done (P), then the configuration on the computer (Q), then devices are connected (R), and finally the speed is tested (S). So the correct sequence is P, Q, R, S.

question.en:
Rearrange the following sentences to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:
P. A large-scale migration was triggered in 1848 by the discovery of gold in California.
Q. Prospectors from all over the world were drawn to the promise of immediate fortune.
R. Few of the "Forty-Niners" did become wealthy.
S. Towns and communities in the American West proliferated as a result of this migration.
[CHSL, 29 Nov 2025, Shift 2]

solution.en: The discovery of gold begins the sequence (P), which attracts prospectors (Q), leading to the growth of towns (S), and finally the observation that only a few became wealthy (R). Thus P, Q, S, R is the most logical order.

question.en:
Rearrange the following sentences to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:
P. The kettle whistled, its steam a thin column in the quiet kitchen.
Q. He placed a teabag in his favourite mug, pouring the hot water over it.
R. A splash of milk clouded the dark liquid, turning it a comforting caramel colour.
S. With the first warm sip, the morning felt a little more manageable.
[CHSL, 30 Nov 2025, Shift 1]

solution.en: The natural sequence is: first the kettle whistles, then hot water is poured into the mug, then milk is added, and finally he takes the first sip. So P-Q-R-S forms the correct paragraph.

question.en:
Rearrange the following sentence parts to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:
P. The research team recruited a large group of qualified participants for the study.
Q. At the end of the trial, they analysed the results to determine the drug's effectiveness.
R. The team monitored the health and progress of all the participants for several months.
S. Half the participants received the new drug, while the other half received a placebo.
[CHSL, 30 Nov 2025, Shift 1]

solution.en: First participants are recruited, then they are divided into drug/placebo groups, then monitored over time, and finally the results are analysed. Therefore, P-S-R-Q is the correct order.

question.en:
**Rearrange the following sentences to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:**

**P.** The last sculpture, a woman carved from one block of marble, had an expression of deep sorrow.
**Q.** For months, the sculptor had worked incessantly, hacking away at the rock.
**R.** She was motivated by a black-and-white photo of her grandmother taken during times of severe hardship.
**S.** The painting was a dedication, a gesture of honouring the memory and the resilience of the woman.
[CHSL, 30 Nov 2025, Shift 3]

solution.en:
The correct sequence is R, Q, P, S. Sentence R introduces the motivation (the photo of the grandmother). Q describes the sculptor's work process. P presents the final sculpture and its expression. S explains the purpose and meaning of the work. This logical flow creates a coherent narrative. Rearranging sentences tests understanding of narrative structure and logical progression. Proper sequencing ensures clarity and coherence in writing.
---

question.en:
**Rearrange the following sentence parts to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:**

**P.** He presented his diagnosis and suggested a course of treatment with assurance.
**Q.** In order to search for particular markers, he ordered a number of imaging scans and blood tests.
**R.** He went over all the information, comparing it to what he knew about medicine.
**S.** As the patient explained their symptoms, the doctor paid close attention.
[CHSL, 30 Nov 2025, Shift 3]

solution.en:
The correct sequence is S, Q, R, P. Sentence S describes the doctor listening to the patient's symptoms (the starting point). Q follows with the doctor ordering tests. R shows the doctor analyzing the information. P concludes with the diagnosis and treatment suggestion. This sequence follows the logical flow of a medical consultation. Understanding chronological and logical order is essential for coherent writing and comprehension.
---

question.en:
Rearrange the following sentences to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:


**P. She used her little trowel to loosen the rich, black dirt.**
**Q. She made a shallow hole and carefully lowered a little seed into it.**
**R. She would now watch for the emergence of the first small sprout.**
**S. The ground was saturated by a soft stream of water, signifying the possibility of fresh life.**

Choose the correct option: [SSC CHSL Tier 1, 12 Nov 2025, Shift-2]
[CHSL, 12 Nov 2025, Shift 2]

solution.en: The logical sequence of planting a seed naturally begins with preparing the soil (P: loosening the dirt), followed directly by the act of planting (Q: making a hole and lowering the seed), then providing hydration (S: saturating the ground with water), and finally the result of waiting for growth (R: watching for the sprout). Thus, PQSR is the most coherent chronological order.

question.en:
Rearrange the following sentence parts to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:


**P. He believed that the id, ego, and superego were all interrelated components of the mind.**
**Q. Sigmund Freud's work greatly shaped our conception of the human mind.**
**R. Unconscious urges often drive our conscious behavior, as per his psychoanalytic theory.**
**S. The conflicts which create psychological distress and worry were explained by this complex paradigm.**

Choose the correct option: [SSC CHSL Tier 1, 12 Nov 2025, Shift-2]
[CHSL, 12 Nov 2025, Shift 2]

solution.en: Sentence Q serves as the perfect introductory statement by introducing the main subject (Sigmund Freud) and the general topic of the human mind. Sentence P naturally follows by detailing his specific beliefs regarding the mind's interrelated components (id, ego, superego). Sentence R expands upon his psychoanalytic theory regarding unconscious urges. Finally, Sentence S concludes the thought by summarizing how **this complex paradigm** effectively explains psychological distress. Therefore, QPRS is the correct flow.

question.en:
Given below are four jumbled parts of a sentence. Select the option that gives their correct order and forms a meaningful sentence.
P. to automate complex tasks that once
Q. Artificial Intelligence has the potential
R. required human intuition and years of specialized training
S. thereby revolutionizing the modern workforce
[CHSL Tier-2]

solution.en: The sentence starts with the subject “Artificial Intelligence,” then “has the potential,” followed by the infinitive phrase and the clause, ending with the result. Learning points: Begin with a complete subject + verb (Q); “to automate…” logically follows “has the potential” (P); “that once required…” modifies “tasks” (R); “thereby…” is a concluding result phrase (S); jumbles are solved by grammar + logical flow.

question.en:
Given below are four jumbled parts of a sentence. Select the option that gives their correct order and forms a meaningful sentence.
P. while providing a platform for global connectivity
Q. can also lead to mental health issues
R. excessive use of social media platforms
S. if not balanced with real-world interactions
[CHSL Tier-2]

solution.en: Correct Answer is option (a) PRQS

question.en:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.
P: In addition, these ancient manuscripts provide profound insights into human consciousness.
Q: Therefore, modern scholars continue to analyze these texts for timeless wisdom.
R: Ancient Indian scriptures offer a vast treasure of philosophical and spiritual knowledge.
S: However, translating these complex Sanskrit verses remains a very difficult task.
[CHSL Tier-2]

solution.en: Start with a general statement (R), add supporting point (P), then contrast with a difficulty (S), and conclude with outcome (Q). Learning points: “In addition” must follow an initial idea; “However” introduces contrast after positives; “Therefore” signals conclusion/result; paragraph coherence depends on connectors; use transition words to order jumbles.

question.en:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.
P: In contrast, applying a heavy moisturizer first would block the absorption of lighter serums.
Q: Hence, layering products from thinnest to thickest consistency ensures maximum efficacy for every ingredient.
R: Typically, a balanced skincare routine begins with a gentle cleanser to remove daily impurities.
S: Additionally, active treatments like vitamin C should be applied directly onto clean, damp skin.
[CHSL Tier-2]

solution.en: A routine begins (R), then adds next step (S), then contrasts with wrong approach (P), and concludes with the guiding principle (Q). Learning points: “Typically” is a natural opener; “Additionally” adds a step after the opener; “In contrast” introduces the caution; “Hence” concludes with the rule; signal words (typically/additionally/in contrast/hence) dictate order.

question.en:
**Which of the given options arranges the following sentences in the most logical sequence to form a meaningful paragraph?**

1. Without keystone species, entire ecosystems can collapse, leading to significant biodiversity loss.
2. The concept of a keystone species was first introduced by ecologist Robert Paine, who studied the effect of removing certain predators from an ecosystem.
3. Keystone species play a disproportionately large role in maintaining the structure and stability of their ecosystems.
4. For example, sea otters help regulate sea urchin populations, preventing the destruction of kelp forests.
5. This idea revolutionized ecology by highlighting how some species have a far greater impact on their environment than others.
[CPO, 09 Dec 2025, Shift 1]

solution.en: Sentence 3 introduces the idea of keystone species. Sentence 2 then explains who introduced the concept. Sentence 5 naturally follows because "This idea" refers to that concept. Sentence 4 gives an example, and sentence 1 concludes with the consequence of losing keystone species. So 3-2-5-4-1 is the best sequence.

question.en:
**Rearrange the following sentences in correct order to make a logical passage.**
1. Employees receive a performance review at the end of each quarter.
2. Based on performance, goals are set for the next quarter.
3. Feedback is provided during the review session.
4. The employees then work towards meeting the set targets.
[CPO, 09 Dec 2025, Shift 1]

solution.en: First, employees receive the review (1). During that review, feedback is given (3). Then goals are set for the next quarter based on performance (2). Finally, employees work towards those targets (4). So 1-3-2-4 is the logical sequence.

question.en:
**Rearrange the following sentences in correct order to make a logical passage.**
1. This leads to a decline in their overall well-being.
2. Many people today suffer from excessive stress.
3. Consequently, coping mechanisms become essential for a balanced life.
4. It often manifests as physical and mental exhaustion.
[CPO, 09 Dec 2025, Shift 1]

solution.en: The paragraph begins with the general statement that many people suffer from excessive stress (2). Then "It" in sentence 4 refers to stress, so 4 follows. This then leads to a decline in well-being (1), and as a result, coping mechanisms become essential (3). Hence, 2-4-1-3 is correct.

question.en:
Which of the following options, rearrange the given sentences in a proper sequence to make a meaningful passage?

1. Johann Wolfgang von Goethe is often regarded as one of the most important figures in German literature and thought.
2. His "Theory of Colours", challenged Isaac Newton's ideas by arguing that colour is not merely a product of light refraction but also influenced by human perception.
3. Goethe was also deeply interested in the sciences and his work in the field of colour theory and plant morphology was groundbreaking in its time.
4. Goethe’s works, such as the Faust plays, explored themes of human desire, ambition, and the quest for knowledge.
5. Goethe also developed the concept of the "Urpflanze" or "primordial plant," suggesting that all plant structures derive from a common, adaptable form.
[CPO, 09 Dec 2025, Shift 2]

solution.en: Sentence 1 introduces Goethe. Sentence 4 follows with his literary work. Sentence 3 shifts to his scientific interests. Sentence 2 gives a specific example from colour theory, and sentence 5 adds another scientific contribution. Hence, 1-4-3-2-5 is coherent.

question.en:
Rearrange the following sentences to form a meaningful passage:
1. Philosophical scepticism questions whether knowledge is possible.
2. This position originated in ancient Greek thought.
3. Later, it influenced Enlightenment thinkers.
4. Its legacy persists in modern epistemology.
[CPO, 09 Dec 2025, Shift 2]

solution.en: Sentence 1 introduces the topic. Sentence 2 explains its origin. Sentence 3 describes later influence, and sentence 4 concludes with its continuing legacy. Thus 1-2-3-4 is the most logical order.

question.en:
Rearrange the following sentences in correct order to make a logical passage.
1. However, it requires careful planning and execution.
2. Launching a new product can be an exciting venture.
3. Market research is the first crucial step to ensure success.
4. This helps in understanding customer needs and competitive landscape.
[CPO, 09 Dec 2025, Shift 2]

solution.en: Sentence 2 introduces the topic. Sentence 1 adds a caution. Sentence 3 gives the first step, and sentence 4 explains the benefit of that step. Therefore, 2-1-3-4 is the correct sequence.

question.en:
Which of the following options, rearrange the given sentences in a proper sequence to make a meaningful passage?

1. English became a global lingua franca, constantly evolving by absorbing words from languages worldwide and adapting to technological and scientific advancements.

2. It was quite different from modern English, with a complex grammar system and a vocabulary influenced by Norse due to Viking invasions.

3. Old English was heavily influenced by Germanic languages brought by the Angles, Saxons, and Jutes in the 5th century.

4. The Renaissance and the invention of the printing press helped standardize English spelling and grammar, leading to the rise of Early Modern English.

5. With the Norman Conquest of 1066, a large number of French and Latin words were incorporated in English, particularly in government, law and art.
[CPO, 10 Dec 2025, Shift 1]

solution.en: The logical order begins with Old English, then describes it, then moves to the Norman influence, then the Renaissance standardization, and finally modern global English.

2. The concept of a keystone species was first introduced by ecologist Robert Paine, who studied the effect of removing certain predators from an ecosystem.

3. Keystone species play a disproportionately large role in maintaining the structure and stability of their ecosystems.

4. For example, sea otters help regulate sea urchin populations, preventing the destruction of kelp forests.

5. This idea revolutionized ecology by highlighting how some species have a far greater impact on their environment than others.
[CPO, 10 Dec 2025, Shift 1]

solution.en: The paragraph should begin with the definition, then mention its origin, then its significance, then an example, and conclude with the consequence of absence.

question.en:
**Which of the given options arranges the following sentences in the most logical sequence to form a meaningful paragraph?**

1. James Watson and Francis Crick, building on Rosalind Franklin’s X-ray diffraction images, proposed the model in 1953.
2. Understanding DNA’s structure has led to developments in medicine, forensic science, and evolutionary research.
3. Their findings demonstrated how DNA stores genetic information through base pairing.
4. This discovery revolutionized biology, paving the way for advances in genetic engineering and biotechnology.
5. The discovery of DNA’s double-helix structure was a major breakthrough in genetics.
[CPO, 10 Dec 2025, Shift 2]

solution.en: Sentence 5 introduces the topic. Sentence 1 tells who made the discovery. Sentence 3 explains what their findings showed. Sentence 4 gives the broader impact, and sentence 2 ends with present-day applications. So 5-1-3-4-2 is the most logical order.

question.en:
Which of the following options, rearrange the given sentences in a proper sequence to make a meaningful passage?

1. The empire's economy also suffered as the Ottomans lost control over key trade routes, particularly with the rise of maritime trade routes controlled by European powers.
2. In the 19th century, the rise of nationalism within the empire's diverse ethnic groups - Greeks, Serbs, Armenians, Arabs, and others - further weakened Ottoman control.
3. The sultans also grew less powerful as the elite bureaucracy became more entrenched, and factionalism within the ruling class created further instability.
4. One of the key factors in the decline of the Ottoman Empire was the weakening of its military forces due to the failure in keeping up with the European military advancements.
5. The final blow came with its involvement in World War I as the Ottomans sided with the Central Powers who were badly defeated by the Allies.
[CPO, 11 Dec 2025, Shift 2]

solution.en: Sentence 4 introduces the topic of Ottoman decline. Sentences 1 and 3 add economic and political/internal weaknesses. Sentence 2 then moves to 19th-century nationalism. Sentence 5 logically concludes with the final blow in World War I. Hence 4-1-3-2-5 is the best sequence.

S2. Someone had said he was "clever," and he had got his invitation in the moderate expectation, on the part of his hostess, that some portion at least of his cleverness would be contributed to the general entertainment.

[GD Constable, 04 May 2026, Shift 1]

A. Having been wounded on the Somme and invalidated out of the Army, I finally took up my quarters with him in London.

B. In doing so, I feel that I cannot do better than begin with that strange tangle which aroused such widespread public interest at the time.

C. Since I have a firsthand knowledge of most of his cases, it has been suggested to me that I select some of the most interesting and place them on record.

D. His success brought him notoriety, and he decided to devote himself to the solving of problems in crime.

S2. I refer to the affair at the Victory Ball.

[GD Constable, 09 May 2026, Shift 1]

solution.en:
The correct sequence is DACB.
S1 introduces Poirot's connection to the Styles Case. 'D' explains the result of his success ("His success brought him notoriety..."). 'A' then introduces the narrator's personal connection ("...I finally took up my quarters with him..."). 'C' explains the reason for writing ("Since I have a firsthand knowledge... it has been suggested to me..."). 'B' then specifies which case he will begin with ("In doing so, I feel that I cannot do better than begin with that strange tangle..."), leading to S2 which names it.
Correct Answer is **DACB** because it follows a logical flow from the subject to the personal connection and then to the purpose.
**Ans: DACB**

B. The party were fond of fish, and Andy and Dave of fishing.
C. However, the creek was low, just a chain of muddy water-holes, from the hole with a few bucketfuls in it to the sizable pool with an average depth of six or seven feet, and they could get fish by bailing out the smaller holes or muddying up the water in the larger ones till the fish rose to the surface.
D. The butcher was always willing to give meat in exchange for fish when they caught more than they could eat; but now it was winter, and these fish wouldn’t bite.
S2. There was the cat-fish, with spikes growing out of the sides of its head, and if you got pricked you’d know it, as Dave said. [MTS, 10 Feb 2025, Shift 1]

solution.en: After listing fish (S1), B introduces the group and their interest in fish/fishing. A logically elaborates on Andy’s fishing behavior. D then adds a seasonal problem (winter; fish wouldn’t bite), which sets up C’s “However” explaining the creek’s low condition and alternative methods to get fish. S2 then continues with a specific description of cat-fish. Learning points: (1) General-to-specific flow improves coherence. (2) Connectives like “However” must contrast something just stated. (3) Background → action → complication → explanation is a common narrative pattern. (4) Keep related details (fishing/bites) grouped.

question.en:
**Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.**

S1. I was rich and contented; I found pleasure in everything that appeals to a man of thirty-five.
A. I married a year ago.
B. A very beautiful, kindly and cultured young lady was my wife.
C. It was a love match.
D. She had been a companion to a countess not far from my estate.
S2. She loved me, and her heart was full of gratitude. [MTS, 10 Feb 2025, Shift 1]

solution.en: A (“I married a year ago.”) naturally begins the marriage detail after S1’s life context. C (“It was a love match.”) follows as a comment on the marriage. B then describes the wife, and D adds her background, leading smoothly to S2 about her love and gratitude. Learning points: (1) Chronology often starts with the event (marriage) then evaluation then description. (2) Pronoun “She” in D needs a clear antecedent (wife) introduced in B. (3) Keep explanatory comments (love match) close to the event. (4) End should support S2’s emotional conclusion.

question.en:
**Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.**

S1. It was long after midnight when we locked up the Englishman and went to bed ourselves.
A. Noble took it very quietly.
B. I having thought of the same thing myself (among many others) said no, because it was more than likely the English wouldn't shoot our men, and anyhow it wasn't to be supposed the Brigade who were always up and down with the second battalion and knew the Englishman well would be likely to want them bumped off.
C. As I blew out the candle I told Noble what Jeremiah Donovan had told me.
D. After we had been in bed about an hour he asked me did I think we ought to tell the Englishmen.
S2. "I think so," says Noble. [MTS, 10 Feb 2025, Shift 2]

solution.en: The logical flow is: after locking up and going to bed (S1), the narrator tells Noble what he heard while blowing out the candle (C). Noble reacts quietly (A). Later, Noble asks whether they should tell the Englishmen (D), and the narrator answers “no” with reasons (B). Finally, Noble concludes, “I think so,” (S2). Learning points: (1) Time markers help: “As I blew out the candle” precedes “After we had been in bed about an hour”. (2) Pronoun reference: “he asked me” needs a prior setup of conversation. (3) Reaction sentence (A) follows the information (C). (4) Long reasoning (B) answers a question (D). (5) Direct speech often closes the paragraph.

question.en:
**Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.**

S1. Then the spring came, and all over the country there were little blossoms and little birds.
A. The only people who were pleased were the Snow and the Frost.
B. Only in the garden of the Selfish Giant it was still winter.
C. The birds did not care to sing in it as there were no children, and the trees forgot to blossom.
D. Once a beautiful flower put its head out from the grass, but when it saw the notice-board it was so sorry for the children that it slipped back into the ground again and went off to sleep.
S2. "Spring has forgotten this garden," they cried, "so we will live here all the year round." [MTS, 10 Feb 2025, Shift 2]

solution.en: After spring arrives everywhere (S1), contrast is introduced: only the Selfish Giant’s garden remains winter (B). Then the effects in the garden are described: birds don’t sing and trees don’t blossom (C). A specific incident follows: a flower appears but retreats on seeing the notice-board (D). Finally, Snow and Frost are pleased and decide to stay (A), leading into their concluding remark in S2. Learning points: (1) Contrast connector: “Only...” naturally follows the general statement about spring. (2) General conditions (C) precede a specific example (D). (3) Snow and Frost being pleased (A) logically comes after winter persists. (4) S2 is direct speech of Snow/Frost, so A should lead into it. (5) Coherence often uses: general → contrast → details → example → conclusion.

question.en:
**Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.**

S1. So why develop your financial genius?
A. I can tell you why I have been developing this area of my intelligence.
B. Not because I need to, but because I want to.
C. Only you can answer that.
D. I do it because I want to make money fast.
S2. It is a fascinating learning process. [MTS, 10 Feb 2025, Shift 3]

solution.en: After S1 (a question), “Only you can answer that” (C) logically responds. Then A introduces the speaker’s explanation (“I can tell you why…”), followed by D giving a reason (money fast), and B refining/qualifying the motive (“Not because… but because…”), ending with S2 as a concluding remark. Other sequences break the question–answer flow or place explanations before the response. Learning points: look for direct replies to questions; identify pronoun reference (“that”); keep cause→clarification order; end with a summarizing sentence.

question.en:
**Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.**

S1. Sofia stood listening to the noise of the departing carriage which bore away her mother and sister.
A. As a child, when some wrong or injustice had been done her, she had cried all alone, in the dark, and the habit had remained with her.
B. She was left alone, quite alone, as she had always wished to be left.
C. Certainly in these moments of complete solitude the consciousness of a great grief came over her;
D. Now, alone in the great drawing room, beneath the brightly lighted chandelier, her hands inert, her head resting against the back of her chair, her face wore an expression of great sorrow, the vivid reflection of a serious inward conflict.
S2. the sentiment of the reality, long repulsed, became clear, distinct, and cruel. [MTS, 10 Feb 2025, Shift 3]

solution.en: After S1, B naturally follows (she is now alone). Then A provides background about her childhood habit of crying alone, supporting the solitude theme. D gives a detailed present scene description (“Now, alone…”), and C transitions into her internal realization of grief, leading into S2’s conclusion. Other orders disrupt the narrative time flow (present scene vs past habit) or weaken the linkage to S2. Learning points: track time markers (“Now,” “As a child”); keep background before detailed present description or as logical support; ensure emotional crescendo to the concluding sentence.

question.en:
**Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered as S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.**

S1. The next morning I went to see her, but when I entered the hut, she, poor thing, was already stark and cold.
A. They were good folk.
B. The babies were left alone.
C. In dying, she had rolled on to this child and crushed her leg.
D. The village folk came to the hut, washed the body, laid her out, made a coffin, and buried her.
S2. What was to be done with them? [MTS, 11 Feb 2025, Shift 1]

solution.en: After S1 reveals the woman is dead, the immediate detail explaining the tragedy is C (she rolled onto the child and crushed her leg). Next, D logically follows as community actions after death (washing, laying out, coffin, burial). Then A provides a general remark about the villagers (“They were good folk”), and B sets up the concluding concern about the children being alone, which leads naturally to S2 (“What was to be done with them?”). Learning points: (1) Look for cause → aftermath → evaluation → problem. (2) Pronoun reference (“them” in S2) must be introduced (babies). (3) Events after death usually precede general commentary. (4) Coherence depends on time order and referents.

question.en:
**Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered as S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.**

S1. One day in autumn on my way back from a remote part of the country I caught cold and fell ill.
A. He prescribed me the usual sudorific, ordered a mustard plaster to be put on, very deftly slid a five-rouble note up his sleeve, coughing drily and looking away as he did so, and then was getting up to go home, but somehow fell into talk and remained.
B. I was exhausted with feverishness; I foresaw a sleepless night and was glad of a little chat with a pleasant companion.
C. Fortunately, the fever attacked me in the district town at the inn; I sent for the doctor.
D. In half an hour the district doctor appeared, a thin, dark-haired man of middle height.
S2. Tea was served. [MTS, 11 Feb 2025, Shift 1]

solution.en: From S1 (fell ill), the next logical step is C (he was in an inn in a district town and sent for the doctor). Then D (doctor arrived). Then A (doctor examined/prescribed and the episode with the note; then he stayed to talk). Then B (narrator’s state and relief at conversation), leading naturally to S2 (tea served). Learning points: (1) Trigger event → action taken → arrival → detailed interaction → reflection. (2) Time marker “In half an hour” must follow “sent for the doctor.” (3) Detailed prescription scene must follow doctor’s arrival. (4) Ending with tea fits after companionship is established.

question.en:
**Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered as S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.**

S1. There was another guest who interested me.
A. He was a personage.
B. At first glance one could tell he was an honoured guest and stood in the same relation to the host as the host to the gentleman of the whiskers.
C. But he was of quite a different order.
D. They called him Julian Mastakovich.
S2. The host and hostess said no end of amiable things to him, were most attentive, wining him, hovering over him, bringing guests up to be introduced, but never leading him to anyone else, [MTS, 11 Feb 2025, Shift 1]

solution.en: After S1 introduces “another guest,” C contrasts him with someone previously mentioned (“a different order”), then A characterizes him (“a personage”), then D gives his name, and B adds how his honoured status was evident at first glance—leading into S2 describing the special attention he received. Learning points: (1) Contrast marker “But” (C) usually comes early after introduction. (2) Naming (D) often follows initial description. (3) Status explanation (B) supports why hosts were attentive in S2. (4) Maintain pronoun clarity: “He” must consistently refer to the same guest.

question.en:
**Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.**

S1. For the first time it occurred to me that if things worked out the way everyone was hoping, I'd be going halfway around the world to live with a man I hadn't even met.
A. It would be ungrateful.
B. Don't send me so far away, I wanted to cry, but of course I didn't.
C. Would I ever see my parents again?
D. Father had worked so hard to find this match for me.
S2. Besides, wasn't it every woman's destiny, as Mother was always telling me, to leave the known for the unknown? [MTS, 11 Feb 2025, Shift 2]

solution.en: The best sequence is CBAD. After S1, the speaker’s immediate worry is about parents (C). Then comes an emotional reaction (B). Next, the speaker checks herself by noting it would be ungrateful (A), and finally gives the reason—father worked hard to find the match (D)—before concluding with S2 about destiny. Learning points: (1) Look for question-to-emotion flow (C → B). (2) “It would be ungrateful” (A) needs a prior impulse to complain (B). (3) “Father had worked…” (D) explains why complaining would be ungrateful. (4) S2 generalises the idea into “destiny,” so it naturally closes. (5) Pronouns and tone shifts help identify coherence.
