Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.**

S1. In the village of Sittendorf in Germany there dwelt, a long time ago, a poor but worthy man whose name was Peter Klaus.
A. He could not have been persuaded for all the money in the world to spend his days in a shop tinkering at a trade.
B. He liked to be out of doors.
C. All the people for miles around knew Peter.
D. He was not fond of hard work.
S2. He liked to wander at his ease in the fields and the woods, enjoying the sunlight and the flowers and the songs of the birds. [MTS, 18 Feb 2025, Shift 3]

solution.en:
C naturally follows the introduction by expanding on Peter’s familiarity; D states his dislike for hard work, A explains that he wouldn’t stay in a shop, and B leads directly into S2 about wandering outdoors.

Why other options are wrong: Other sequences place “out of doors” too early or insert the shop-detail before stating his general attitude toward work, reducing coherence.

Learning points: (1) After introducing a person, a general remark often follows (C). (2) General trait (D) → supporting detail (A). (3) “Out of doors” (B) should connect smoothly to S2’s outdoor wandering. (4) Prefer general-to-specific order. (5) Look for sentences that act as bridges to S2.

question.en:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.
S1. My real life is the one nobody talks about anymore, except Father Paul LeBoeuf, another old buck.
A. But I can't get him on a horse anymore.
B. His face is ruddy, and he jokes about being a whiskey priest, though he's not.
C. He has a decade on me; he's sixty-four, a big man, bald on top with grey at the sides; when he had hair, it was black.
D. He gets outdoors as much as he can, goes for a long walk every morning, and hunts and fishes with me.
S2. Ten years ago I could badger him into a trail ride; I had to give him a western saddle, and he'd hold the pummel and bounce through the woods with me, and be sore for days. [MTS, 19 Feb 2025, Shift 1]

solution.en:
The sequence CBDA is coherent: C introduces who Father Paul is (age/appearance), B adds descriptive detail (ruddy face/jokes), D describes his current activities with the narrator, and A contrasts by noting he can’t be put on a horse anymore—leading smoothly into S2 about trail rides ten years ago.

Why other options are wrong: Other sequences either place the contrast (A) too early or break the descriptive flow from identity → traits → activities → contrast before the past reference in S2.

Learning points: (1) Start with identification/background (often sentence with age/description). (2) Follow with additional traits/details. (3) Then actions/habits. (4) Place contrast words like “But” after some build-up. (5) Use S2 as a timeline anchor.

question.en:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.
S1. The word pronounced by the eccentric veteran seemed to have a magical effect on the rest of the company present.
A. Probably they had expected to profit by my intoxication; but finding that my new friend was benevolently bent on preventing me from getting dead drunk, had now abandoned all hope of this, and retired to enjoy themselves.
B. When the old soldier returned and sat down again opposite to me at the table, we had the room to ourselves.
C. Whatever their motive might be, at any rate they went away in a body.
D. With one accord they all rose to depart.
S2. I could see the croupier, in a sort of vestibule which opened out of it, eating his supper in solitude. [MTS, 19 Feb 2025, Shift 1]

solution.en:
The sequence DACB works best: D shows the immediate reaction (they rose to depart), A gives the reason/assumption about their motive, C generalises the outcome (they went away together), and B states the resulting situation (room to ourselves), which leads naturally into S2 observing the croupier alone.

Why other options are wrong: Starting with B or C before the departure action (D) weakens cause–effect flow; A fits better after the departure is mentioned as an explanation of why they left.

Learning points: (1) Look for “action first” lines after a trigger in S1. (2) Explanations (“Probably…”) often follow the action. (3) Summary lines (“Whatever… at any rate…”) consolidate. (4) Consequence lines (“we had the room…”) set up S2. (5) Maintain time order.

question.en:
**Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.**

S1. For several weeks before Christmas, my father worked after supper in the cellar of our house.
A. My brother Laird and I sat on the top step and watched.
B. The naked, slippery bodies were collected in a sack and buried in the dump.
C. My father removed the pelt inside-out from the body of the fox, which looked surprisingly small, mean, and rat-like, deprived of its arrogant weight of fur.
D. The cellar was whitewashed and lit by a hundred-watt bulb over the worktable.
S2. One time the hired man, Henry Bailey, had taken a swipe at me with this sack, saying, "Christmas present!" [MTS, 19 Feb 2025, Shift 2]

solution.en:
“DACB” creates a coherent flow: setting description (D) → observers (A) → action detail (C) → disposal/result (B), before concluding with S2 referring to “this sack.”

Why other options are wrong: Other sequences disrupt reference continuity (especially the introduction of “this sack”) and break the logical progression from setting to action to outcome.

Learning points: (1) Start with setting/context after S1 when given. (2) Maintain pronoun/reference links (e.g., “this sack”). (3) Prefer chronological action order. (4) Ensure each sentence naturally leads to the next. (5) Check cohesion through repeated nouns (cellar, sack, bodies).

question.en:
**Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.**

S1. Although he was married, with children, his was a solitary disposition; he liked best to work alone.
A. Autumn was best for this, better than spring.
B. It pleased him when he was given a bank to build up or a gate to mend at the far end of the peninsula, where the sea surrounded the farmland on either side.
C. Then, at midday, he would pause and eat the pasty that his wife had baked for him and, sitting on the cliff's edge, would watch the birds.
D. In spring the birds flew inland, purposefully, intent; they knew where they were bound; the rhythm and ritual of their life brooked no delay.
S2. In autumn those that had not migrated overseas but remained to pass the winter were caught up in the same driving urge, but because migration was denied them, followed a pattern of their own. [MTS, 19 Feb 2025, Shift 2]

solution.en:
“BCAD” is coherent: B explains the kind of work he liked; C continues with his midday routine; A introduces that autumn suited this; D contrasts with spring bird behavior, leading naturally to S2 about autumn birds’ different pattern.

Why other options are wrong: Other orders introduce “autumn/spring” comparisons without setup or break the seasonal contrast needed before S2.

Learning points: (1) Look for time markers: “Then,” “Autumn,” “In spring.” (2) Place “Then” after an activity is introduced. (3) Seasonal contrast must be built before a seasonal conclusion. (4) Ensure S2’s “In autumn…” is prepared by earlier autumn references. (5) Coherence depends on logical narrative flow.

S1. The staircase window having been boarded up, no light came down into the hall.
A. Now the prosaic woman, looking about her, was more perplexed than she knew by everything that she saw, by traces of her long former habit of life-the yellow smoke stain up the white marble mantelpiece, the ring left by a vase on the top of the escritoire; the bruise in the wallpaper where, on the door being thrown open widely, the China handle had always hit the wall.
B. Though not much dust had seeped in, each object wore a film of another kind; and, the only ventilation being the chimney, the whole drawing room smelled of the cold hearth.
C. But one door, she could just see, stood ajar, so she went quickly through into the room and unshuttered the big window in there.
D. The piano, having gone away to be stored, had left what looked like claw marks on its part of the parquet.
S2. Mrs. Drover put down her parcels on the escritoire and left the room to proceed upstairs; the things she wanted were in a bedroom chest. [MTS, 19 Feb 2025, Shift 2]

solution.en:
“CADB” fits best: C moves the action into the room and opens the window; A and D detail what she notices inside; B adds atmosphere and condition of the room, leading to S2 where she uses the escritoire and leaves upstairs.

Why other options are wrong: Other sequences either start with detailed observations before the entry/action (C) or place atmospheric description in a way that interrupts the observation flow.

Learning points: (1) Action/movement sentences often precede detailed descriptions. (2) Keep observation details grouped (A, D). (3) Place general atmosphere (B) after key visuals are introduced. (4) Ensure S2 references (escritoire) align with earlier mention. (5) Coherence is built by spatial progression: hall → room → observations.

question.en:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

**S1.** The grandmother didn't want to go to Florida.
**A.** Bailey was the son she lived with, her only boy.
**B.** "Now look here, Bailey," she said, "see here, read this," and she stood with one hand on her thin hip and the other rattling the newspaper at his bald head.
**C.** He was sitting on the edge of his chair at the table, bent over the orange sports section of the Journal.
**D.** She wanted to visit some of her connections in east Tennessee and she was seizing at every chance to change Bailey's mind.
**S2.** "Here this fellow that calls himself The Misfit is aloose from the Federal Pen and headed toward Florida and you read here what it says he did to these people. [MTS, 20 Feb 2025, Shift 1]

solution.en:
The correct sequence is DACB. After S1 introduces the grandmother's reluctance to go to Florida, sentence D explains why—she wanted to visit Tennessee and tried to change Bailey's mind. A introduces Bailey as her only son. C describes Bailey sitting at the table reading the newspaper. B shows the grandmother trying to convince him by rattling the newspaper at him. This flows naturally into S2 where she mentions The Misfit.

Why other options are wrong: CBDA, BDAC, and ACBD do not maintain logical narrative flow. The grandmother's motivation (D) should come before identifying Bailey (A), followed by the scene description (C) and her action (B).

Learning points: (1) Start with motivation before action. (2) Introduce characters before describing their actions. (3) Physical descriptions precede dialogue. (4) Chronological order matters in narrative sequencing. (5) The final sentence should connect smoothly with S2.

The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.**

S1. Then, one day, she was up, playing; Isabel was in the kitchen fixing lunch for the two boys when they'd come in from school, and she heard Grace fall down in the living room.
A. And she ran to the living room and there was little Grace on the floor, all twisted up, and the reason she hadn't screamed was that she couldn't get her breath.
B. When you have a lot of children you don't always start running when one of them falls, unless they start screaming or something.
C. Yet, Isabel says that when she heard that thump and then that silence, something happened in her to make her afraid.
D. And, this time, Grace was quiet.
S2. And when she did scream, it was the worst sound, Isabel says, that she'd ever heard in all her life, and she still hears it sometimes in her dreams. [MTS, 20 Feb 2025, Shift 2]

solution.en:
The logical flow is: general situation (B) → unusual silence (D) → fear due to thump and silence (C) → scene in living room explaining why no scream yet (A), before S2 mentions the eventual scream.

Why other options are wrong: Other sequences misplace the general statement (B) or the “this time” reference (D), breaking coherence and cause-effect progression.

Learning points: (1) Place general statements early to set context. (2) “This time” must follow a comparison/context. (3) Cause-effect: thump+silence → fear → discovery. (4) Pronoun/reference tracking improves ordering. (5) Ensure S2’s “when she did scream” is prepared by “couldn’t get her breath.”

Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.**

S1. In old times there was a certain petty monarch by the name of Jayadatta, and there was born to him a son named Devadatta.
A. Therefore, I will take a wife to my son from a merchant's family, in order that misfortune may not overtake his throne, though it is surrounded with many relations."
B. "The prosperity of kings is very unstable, being like a courtesan to be enjoyed by force; but the prosperity of merchants is like a woman of good family; it is steady and does not fly to another man."
C. And that wise king, wishing to marry his son, who was grown up, thus reflected:
D. Having formed this resolve, that king sought for his son the daughter of a merchant in Pataliputra named Vasudatta.
S2. Vasudatta for his part, eager for such a distinguished alliance, gave that daughter of his to the prince, though he dwelt in a remote foreign land. [MTS, 20 Feb 2025, Shift 2]

solution.en:
After introduction (S1), the king reflects (C), then gives the reasoning about merchants vs kings (B), then concludes the decision (A), and finally acts on it by seeking Vasudatta (D), leading to S2.

Why other options are wrong: Starting with B without “thus reflected” (C) lacks setup; placing D too early introduces the action before the decision is stated.

Learning points: (1) Reflection/setup lines often precede quoted reasoning. (2) A decision (“Therefore…”) follows reasons. (3) Actions (“Having formed this resolve…”) follow decisions. (4) Maintain logical chronology: think → decide → act. (5) Use connectors like “Therefore” and “Having formed this resolve” as ordering clues.

question.en:

question.en:

question.en:
Which of the given options is the most logical sequencing of the following sentences to form a meaningful paragraph?

Sentence 2 (So, we must take care of our plants) follows as the action needed.
Sentence 4 (Then, our plants will be healthy) describes the positive outcome.

**Dislodge (हटाना/बाहर निकालना)** = to remove or force out from a position. The sentence requires a verb that can act upon "entrenched bureaucratic inertia," implying forceful removal.
**Persuade (मनाना)** = to convince → does not fit the context of removing inertia.
**Dislodge (हटाना)** = to force out → fits perfectly.
**Dissuasion (निरुत्साहन)** = the act of discouraging → is a noun, not a verb.
**Disillusion (मोहभंग)** = to disappoint or disenchant → does not fit.
Correct Answer is **dislodge** because it means to forcibly remove something from a fixed position.
**Ans: dislodge**

**Quell (दबाना/शांत करना)** = to suppress or put an end to. The sentence describes a veiled attempt to suppress dissent.
**Quell (दबाना)** = to suppress → fits the context of suppressing dissent.
**Swell (बढ़ाना)** = to increase → is opposite.
**Rebut (खंडन करना)** = to argue against → does not mean to suppress.
**Impugn (संदेह करना)** = to challenge or question → does not fit.
Correct Answer is **quell** because it means to suppress or subdue, which fits the context of suppressing dissent.
**Ans: quell**

**Address (संबोधित करना/निपटाना)** = to deal with or discuss a topic. The sentence states the rebuttal failed to deal with the central issue.
**Address (निपटाना)** = to deal with → fits the context.
**Digress (विषयांतर करना)** = to stray from the topic → is opposite of addressing.
**Circumvent (टालना/बायपास करना)** = to avoid dealing with → is the opposite.
**Elude (बच निकलना)** = to escape or avoid → is the opposite.
Correct Answer is **address** because it means to deal with or tackle an issue directly.
**Ans: address**

**Nevertheless (तथापि/फिर भी)** = introduces a contrasting point. The sentence contrasts a compelling argument with the fact that it was based on outdated data.
**Otherwise (अन्यथा)** = introduces an alternative condition → doesn't fit.
**Conversely (विलोमतः)** = indicates a reversal → doesn't fit.
**Nevertheless (फिर भी)** = introduces a contrast → fits perfectly.
**Subsequently (बाद में)** = indicates time sequence → doesn't fit.
Correct Answer is **nevertheless** because it correctly introduces a contrasting idea to the previous clause.
**Ans: nevertheless**

**Devolved (पतित होना/बिगड़ना)** = to degenerate or deteriorate into a worse state. The sentence implies the discussion could have deteriorated into a stalemate.
**Evolved (विकसित होना)** = to develop gradually → implies positive progression, opposite.
**Devolved (बिगड़ना)** = to degenerate → fits the context of worsening.
**Emerged (उभरना)** = to come out → doesn't imply deterioration.
**Absorbed (अवशोषित)** = to take in → is irrelevant.
Correct Answer is **devolved** because it means to degenerate or decline into a worse condition.
**Ans: devolved**

question.en:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
The government's new policies sought to _________ economic growth, not stifle it. [CGL, 14 Oct 2025, Shift 2]

solution.en:
**Stimulate (प्रोत्साहित करना)** = to encourage or spur activity. The sentence states the policies sought to encourage growth, not stifle it.
**Hinder (बाधा डालना)** = to obstruct → is the opposite.
**Impede (रोकना)** = to hinder → is the opposite.
**Stimulate (प्रोत्साहित करना)** = to encourage → fits the context.
**Curtail (कम करना)** = to reduce → is the opposite.
Correct Answer is **stimulate** because it means to encourage or spur economic growth, which is the opposite of stifling it.
**Ans: stimulate**

**Opposed (विरोधी)** = in conflict or contrast with something. The phrase "diametrically opposed" means completely opposite.
**Adverse (प्रतिकूल)** = harmful/unfavorable → doesn't fit "diametrically".
**Averse (अनिच्छुक)** = having a strong dislike → doesn't mean direct opposition.
**Converse (विलोम)** = reversed in order → doesn't describe direct opposition.
**Opposed (विरोधी)** = in direct contrast → fits perfectly with "diametrically".
Correct Answer is **opposed** because it means in direct conflict or contrast with something, fitting the phrase "diametrically opposed."
**Ans: opposed**

question.en: Although the experiment had been meticulously designed, unforeseen variables ____ the reliability of its conclusions. [CGL, 15 Sep 2025, Shift 3]

solution.en:
**Undermined (कमजोर करना)** = to weaken or reduce the effectiveness. The sentence says unforeseen variables negatively impacted reliability.
**Undermined (कमजोर करना)** = to weaken → fits the context.
**Bolstered (मजबूत करना)** = to support/strengthen → is opposite.
**Ratified (पुष्टि करना)** = to formally approve → doesn't fit.
**Exacerbated (बढ़ाना/खराब करना)** = to make worse → doesn't specifically mean to weaken reliability in this context.
Correct Answer is **undermined** because it means to weaken or reduce the effectiveness of something.
**Ans: undermined**

question.en:
<strong>Select the correct option: </strong><br />
The artifact was notable not merely for its age but also for the ____ with which it was preserved. [CGL, 16 Sep 2025, Shift 1]

solution.en:

**Meticulousness (सावधानी)** = extreme care → fits the context of preservation.
**Velocity (गति)** = speed → irrelevant.
**Brevity (संक्षिप्तता)** = shortness → irrelevant.
**Severity (गंभीरता)** = harshness → irrelevant.
Correct Answer is **meticulousness** because it means extreme care and attention to detail, which fits the context of preservation.

question.en:
<strong>Select the correct option: </strong><br />
Only after years of archival research did the historian manage to ____ the contradictory accounts of the regime&#39;s collapse. [CGL, 16 Sep 2025, Shift 3]

solution.en:
**Reconcile (समाधान करना/मेल करना)** = to make consistent or harmonize conflicting ideas. The sentence says the historian harmonized contradictory accounts.
**Retract (वापस लेना)** = to withdraw → doesn't fit.
**Revise (संशोधित करना)** = to change/modify → doesn't imply harmonizing contradictions.
**Reconcile (मेल करना)** = to harmonize → fits perfectly.
**Reverberate (गूंजना)** = to echo → irrelevant.
Correct Answer is **reconcile** because it means to harmonize or make conflicting accounts consistent.
**Ans: reconcile**

**Disregarded (अनदेखा किया गया)** = ignored or not given importance. Controversial findings are likely to be initially ignored.
**Disregarded (अनदेखा)** = ignored → fits the context of controversy.
**Celebrated (प्रशंसित)** = praised → opposite.
**Acclaimed (सराहा गया)** = praised → opposite.
**Adopted (अपनाया गया)** = accepted → opposite.
Correct Answer is **disregarded** because it means ignored, which fits the context of controversial findings being initially rejected.
**Ans: disregarded**

**Deterrent (निवारक/रोक)** = something that discourages or prevents an action. The intervention was aimed at preventing escalating tensions.
**Deterrent (निवारक)** = a discouragement → fits the context.
**Detention (नजरबंदी)** = confinement → doesn't fit.
**Detraction (अपमान)** = belittling → doesn't fit.
**Derision (उपहास)** = mockery → doesn't fit.
Correct Answer is **deterrent** because it means something that discourages or prevents an action, fitting the context of preventing tensions.
**Ans: deterrent**

question.en: <div><strong>Select the correct option:</strong> Far from being a liability, his dissenting views often served as a ____ to complacency within the group.</div> [CGL, 20 Sep 2025, Shift 1]

solution.en:
**Counterweight (संतुलन/प्रतिसंतुलन)** = a force or influence that balances or counteracts something. Dissenting views balanced complacency.

**Detriment (हानि)** = harm → opposite.
**Digression (विषयांतर)** = deviation → irrelevant.
**Repudiation (अस्वीकृति)** = rejection → doesn't fit.
Correct Answer is **counterweight** because it means a balancing force against complacency.
**Ans: counterweight**

question.en:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate verb:

**Suppressed (दबाया)** = subdued → doesn't fit.

question.en:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option:
The novel's protagonist is portrayed as a ______ hero, flawed yet striving for redemption.

**Quixotic (आदर्शवादी/अव्यावहारिक)** = idealistic and impractical → doesn't fit "flawed".
**Fallible (त्रुटियों वाला)** = capable of making mistakes → fits "flawed".

question.en:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option:
The legislation was passed with ______ support, uniting parties across the political spectrum.





[CHSL, 24 Nov 2025, Shift 2]

solution.en:
**Unanimous (सर्वसम्मत)** = fully in agreement. The sentence says it united parties across the spectrum.
**Partisan (पक्षपाती)** = biased toward one side → opposite.

question.en: <div class="q-context-preview"><span style="caret-color: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0);">In the following question, a sentence with a blank is given, followed by five words labeled (1), (2), (3), (4), and (5). The pursuit of space exploration (1) ____ not merely an extension of scientific curiosity but a profound statement about humanity's aspirations and existential resilience. Beyond the immediate technological marvels, space missions foster unprecedented advancements in materials science, medicine, and artificial intelligence, all of which invariably (3) ____ civilian life on Earth. However, venturing into the cosmos is fraught with ethical dilemmas. Questions surrounding planetary protection—ensuring that alien ecosystems are neither contaminated nor exploited, remain largely (4) nascent within international law. Moreover, the colossal costs of space programs provoke debates about distributive justice, particularly in a world where basic human needs remain unmet for millions. solution.en:
**Rule: Subject-Verb Agreement. The head of the subject is the main noun in the subject phrase.**
The subject is "The pursuit of space exploration". The headword is "pursuit", which is a singular noun. Therefore, the verb must be singular. In the present tense, the singular form of "represent" is "represents".
The other options are either plural ("represent"), a participle ("representing"), or in the wrong tense ("represented").
Correct Answer is **represents** because the singular subject "pursuit" requires a singular verb.
**Ans: represents**

question.en: <div class="q-context-preview"><span style="caret-color: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0);">In the following question, a sentence with a blank is given, followed by five words labeled (1), (2), (3), (4), and (5). Choose the word that fills the blank appropriately in the context of the passage. The pursuit of space exploration (1) ____ not merely an extension of scientific curiosity but a profound statement about humanity's aspirations and existential resilience. As Earth's resources dwindle and environmental degradation escalates the imperative to seek alternative habitats (2) ____ increasingly unavoidable. Beyond the immediate technological marvels, space missions foster unprecedented advancements in materials science, medicine, and artificial intelligence, all of which invariably (3) ____ civilian life on Earth. However, venturing into the cosmos is fraught with ethical dilemmas. Questions surrounding planetary protection—ensuring that alien ecosystems are neither contaminated nor exploited, remain largely (4) nascent within international law. Moreover, the colossal costs of space programs provoke debates about distributive justice, particularly in a world where basic human needs remain unmet for millions. Thus, a responsible trajectory of space exploration must harmonize ambition with stewardship, (5) tempering technological triumphalism with humility. Ultimately, the future of humanity may indeed lie among the stars, but whether that future is marked by expansionist hubris or enlightened coexistence will depend on the philosophical frameworks we choose to uphold in these uncharted domains. </span></div><div>In this context, &#39;nascent&#39; most nearly means: (4)</div> [CGL, 25 Sep 2025, Shift 1]

solution.en:
"Nascent" (नवजात/विकासोन्मुख) means something that is just coming into existence. It is often used to describe something in its early, developing stages.
"Well-established" is the opposite. "Deliberately hidden" and "Declining rapidly" are unrelated.
Correct Answer is **Primitive or newly developing** because nascent refers to the early stage of development.
**Ans: Primitive or newly developing**

**Rule: Subject-Verb Agreement. The head of the subject must be identified.**
The subject is "virtual realms". The headword is "realms", which is plural. Therefore, the verb must be plural. The present continuous plural form is "are beginning to".
The other options are either singular, in the past tense, or do not match the subject.
Correct Answer is **are beginning to** because the plural subject "realms" requires a plural verb.
**Ans: are beginning to**

**Rule: Subject-Verb Agreement. The verb must agree with the main noun in the subject phrase.**
The subject is "overreliance on synthetic environments". The headword is "overreliance", which is a singular noun. Therefore, the verb must be singular. The present tense singular form of "erode" is "erodes".
The other options are either plural, in the past tense, or a participle.
Correct Answer is **erodes** because the singular subject "overreliance" requires a singular verb.
**Ans: erodes**

"Liminality" (सीमांतता) refers to a transitional or threshold state, being in-between two different states.
"A state of fixed certainty" is the opposite. "A complete loss of boundaries" is too extreme. "An ultimate destination" is the opposite of a transitional state.
Correct Answer is **a transitional or threshold state** because liminality refers to a state of being 'in between'.
**Ans: a transitional or threshold state**

**Rule: Subject-Verb Agreement.**
The subject is "the imperative to cultivate critical consciousness". The headword is "imperative", which is a singular noun. Therefore, the verb must be singular. The singular form of "remain" is "remains".
The other options are either plural, in the past tense, or a participle.
Correct Answer is **remains** because the singular subject "imperative" requires a singular verb.
**Ans: remains**

"Sisyphean" (सीज़ीफ़ियन/व्यर्थ और अनंत) refers to a task that is laborious, futile, and endless, much like the myth of Sisyphus.
"Triumphant and rewarding" is the opposite. "Spontaneous and accidental" and "Structured and linear" do not capture the nature of a futile, repetitive task.
Correct Answer is **futile and endless** because the allusion to Sisyphus means a task that is both difficult and endless.
**Ans: futile and endless**

In the following question, some of the words in the passage have been left out. Read the passage carefully and choose the correct word for each blank, out of the four alternatives and fill in the blanks.
After falling consistently ________ (1) the U.S. dollar for a major part of the year, the rupee has ________ (2) somewhat over the last few weeks. It has risen by almost 15% from its lowest levels ________ (3) in October. Even with this recent improvement, the rupee is still down about 11% since the start of the year. The rupee's performance has been closely ________ (4) to global crude oil prices. This makes sense, as imported oil accounts for about 80% of India's total demand. The value of the rupee dropped when oil prices climbed earlier this year, a trend that lasted until early October. Since then, as global crude prices have fallen, the rupee has ________ (5) against the dollar.

What should come in blank (1)?
[CGL Tier-2]

solution.en:
The correct collocation is “falling consistently against the U.S. dollar,” which means losing value in comparison to the dollar. The other prepositions do not fit this economic expression.
Learning points:
- “against” is commonly used with currency comparison
- “rise/fall against a currency” is standard financial usage
- Contextual collocation is key in cloze tests

In the given passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage intently and choose the most appropriate option to fill in each blank:
Democracies are usually credited with being resilient, yet the past indicates that they can be quite vulnerable. Those institutions that are meant to protect freedom can weaken when citizens become disconnected or when politicians take advantage of (1) ______ within the system. Gradual removal of checks and balances might not raise an alarm until it is too late.

One of the central factors is the state of public discourse. When argument gets polarised and facts are sacrificed to (2) ______, democratic conventions start to disintegrate. The media is responsible here, either as a watchdog or as a megaphone for disinformation. The advent of echo chambers has made it simpler for individuals to shun (3) ______ perspectives, strengthening tribalism.

Economic inequality is another threat. When significant portions of the populace feel left out of prosperity, they can lose confidence in democratic processes and seek (4) ______ alternatives. This cynicism can be taken advantage of by populist movements that make quick fixes but destroy democratic ideas.

Democracy must be safeguarded with vigilance, participation, and a willingness to search for truth. Without these, even the most entrenched systems can become (5) ______ susceptible to rot from within.

What should come in the place of blank number 1?
[CHSL Tier-2]

solution.en: “Take advantage of gaps within the system” is the natural collocation and best fits the meaning. Learning points: “Gap” commonly pairs with “in the system”; context clues: politicians exploit weaknesses/loopholes; eliminate words that don’t collocate (take advantage of balances/strength); blanks often test collocation; read the full sentence before choosing.

Equity in education is not a matter of distributing identical tools to unequal lives. It is, instead, the (1) _____ of design—one that begins by listening, not prescribing. To mistake uniformity for fairness is to ignore the histories etched into the margins of classrooms: the quiet absence of confidence, the inherited silences of caste, class, or gender, the invisible weight of underfed attention. In this context, merit is often brandished as a (2) _____, obscuring the scaffolded advantages that shape who arrives prepared and who arrives late. That redrawing requires more than infrastructure—it demands a (3) _____ of imagination. What if assessments accounted for lived complexity? What if pedagogy paused for breath where society gasps for access? Education is not a ladder out of poverty if the rungs are greased for some and splintered for others. Nor is inclusion real if it is merely spatial—a desk, a roll call, a token smile. True equity emerges not from programs alone, but from the (4) _____ to confront whose stories are centred, whose questions are validated, and whose silences are allowed to remain unbroken. The future of learning lies not in acceleration, but in the willingness to (5) _____ where we have failed to ask why the answers always sound the same.

What should come in the place of blank number (1)?
[CPO, 09 Dec 2025, Shift 2]

solution.en: “Architecture of design” fits the abstract, structural sense intended in the passage. The other options do not fit the phrase or meaning.

Bridging the gap between awareness and action is crucial to empowering women and fostering healthier generations.

solution.en: The phrase "often resulting from" is the correct participial construction modifying "concern." The other forms do not fit grammatically in this context.

In the archipelago of epistemic fracture, where coherence is a relic and continuity a performative illusion, cognition unfolds not through linear causality but via stochastic pulses of informational detritus. Within this disjunctive matrix, agency is less a property of autonomous will than a side effect of algorithmic interpellation. Every action is (1)____ not as a result of volition but as an emergent behavior—calculated, inferred, and subtly modulated by systems of predictive design. In this regime, dissent is not censored but (3)____—subtly realigned to serve the centripetal logics of monetized attention. The archive is not a memory but a battleground: past and present re-stitched according to the dictates of data retention, compliance heuristics, and platformed ontology. What remains is not truth but latency: the delay between perception and its (4)____ by computational governance. Thus, power no longer manifests through prohibition, but through calibration—redefining the limits of thinkability itself. In this techno-psychic schema, liberation is not absent but (5)____: detectable only in its strategic simulation.


What should come in the place of blank number (1)?
[CPO, 10 Dec 2025, Shift 2]

solution.en: The passage says action is produced as an emergent, calculated behavior. **Instantiated** means brought into actual form or made concrete, which best fits this technical context. The others do not match the idea of system-generated behavior.

Initially, the technology (2) _____ largely to religious texts, yet within decades, its reach encompassed scientific treatises, political pamphlets, and literary works. The printing press not only democratized access to information but also catalyzed movements such as the Reformation and the Enlightenment, creating (3) palpable shifts in societal structures.

As books became more affordable and literacy rates rose, ideas could traverse borders with unprecedented speed, challenging established authorities and inspiring intellectual revolutions. What had once been the domain of the few now became a vibrant public discourse, reshaping collective consciousness.

However, the rise of printed material also (4) engendered anxieties among elites, who feared the erosion of traditional hierarchies. Even today, as digital media dominates, the legacy of the printing press (5) _____, underlining the enduring significance of mass communication technologies.

Which tense/form fits best? (1)
[CPO, 11 Dec 2025, Shift 2]

solution.en: The sentence refers to a completed historical event: "The invention of the printing press in the 15th century marked...". The simple past "marked" fits grammatically and contextually. "Was marked" changes the meaning, "marks" is present tense, and "was marking" is awkward here.

In the following question, a sentence with a blank is given, followed by five words labeled (1), (2), (3), (4), and (5). Choose the word that fills the blank appropriately in the context of the passage.

The invention of the printing press in the 15th century (1) _____, heralding a seismic transformation in the dissemination of knowledge across Europe and beyond. Initially, the technology (2) _____ largely to religious texts, yet within decades, its reach encompassed scientific treatises, political pamphlets, and literary works. The printing press not only democratized access to information but also catalyzed movements such as the Reformation and the Enlightenment, creating (3) palpable shifts in societal structures.

As books became more affordable and literacy rates rose, ideas could traverse borders with unprecedented speed, challenging established authorities and inspiring intellectual revolutions. What had once been the domain of the few now became a vibrant public discourse, reshaping collective consciousness.

However, the rise of printed material also (4) engendered anxieties among elites, who feared the erosion of traditional hierarchies. Even today, as digital media dominates, the legacy of the printing press (5) _____, underlining the enduring significance of mass communication technologies.

Which tense/modal suits the idea of continuous influence best? (5)
[CPO, 11 Dec 2025, Shift 2]

solution.en: The sentence connects past legacy to the present: "Even today... the legacy of the printing press has endured". The present perfect expresses continuity from past to present. "Endures" is possible in ordinary usage, but the marked correct option in the source is "has endured."

question.en:
Read the passage and answer the following question(s):

In the given passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage intently and choose the most appropriate option to fill in each blank:

Somewhere between the glint of touchscreen interfaces and the blur of algorithmic suggestion lies a silent erosion of pause. The modern subject, once presumed to be an agent of reflection, increasingly becomes a vessel for speed—tethered not to thought, but to reflex. What is offered as efficiency often exacts a toll in deliberation. Every frictionless swipe and curated feed removes the texture of decision, substituting it with a stream of optimized compulsions. The interface smiles, but never waits. In this schema, slowness becomes suspect, and interruption is an error to be patched. As platforms preempt intent, they also unmake it: the user acts, but only within corridors already anticipated. In such a world, the idea of freedom becomes (1) _____, not in absence, but in excess—drowned in choice yet starved of consequence. If autonomy is to mean more than responsive motion, we must recover the grammar of refusal. The act of pausing, once mundane, is now almost (2) _____, a resistance against the coercive design of continuity. Regulation, in this context, is not merely about protection; it is about preserving (3) _____ in a system that privileges momentum over mindfulness. We do not need more personalization—we need more interruption. Only by interrupting the velocity of interface can we hope to return to the interiority that once defined being. In this landscape, the measure of health is not how swiftly we act, but how often we are willing to (4) _____ acting. And perhaps, how fiercely we defend the strange dignity of being (5) _____.

What should come in the place of blank number (1)?
[CPO, 11 Dec 2025, Shift 2]

solution.en: The line says freedom is "drowned in choice yet starved of consequence," suggesting that it appears real but is not truly real. "Illusory" best captures this false appearance of freedom.

question.en:
Read the passage below and choose the correct word for each blank.

Cultural heritage reflects the values, traditions, and achievements of a community passed down through generations. It includes monuments, festivals, languages, art, and even traditional knowledge. Preserving heritage is essential, as it helps people stay (1)________ to their roots and identity. However, modernization and urban development often lead to the neglect or destruction of historical sites. Many ancient structures are left unattended, while some cultural practices are forgotten. Governments and citizens must take joint (2)________ to protect such legacies. Promoting local art, restoring monuments, and teaching indigenous history in schools are effective ways to keep heritage alive. Tourists should also behave (3)________ when visiting culturally sensitive locations. Heritage preservation is not only about remembering the past, but also about inspiring future generations with a sense of (4)________ and continuity. Losing heritage means losing the story of a people, and that is a loss that cannot be easily (5)________.

(1)
[CPO, 12 Dec 2025, Shift 1]

solution.en: The phrase "connected to their roots and identity" is the natural and meaningful expression in the context of heritage preservation.

question.en:
Read the passage below and choose the correct word for each blank.

The rapid adoption of digital tools has revolutionized the field of education. Online platforms, interactive modules, and virtual classrooms have made learning more accessible and (1)_______ for students around the world. These technologies allow learners to progress at their own pace, revisit difficult concepts, and explore subjects beyond traditional syllabi. However, digital learning also brings certain challenges. Not all students have equal access to reliable internet or digital (2)_______, which creates a significant learning gap. Moreover, prolonged screen time and lack of real-world interaction can affect both physical health and social development. To address these issues, institutions must adopt a blended approach—one that combines the flexibility of digital content with the structure of face-to-face learning. Teachers must also be trained to effectively integrate technology into the classroom, ensuring that it enhances rather than (3)_______ the learning process. When used responsibly, digital education has the potential to (4)_______ barriers and bring quality instruction to even the most remote corners of the world. But for it to be truly effective, students must stay disciplined, motivated, and (5)_______ in their learning journey.

(1)
[CPO, 12 Dec 2025, Shift 2]

solution.en:
In the context of the passage, "personalized" is the most appropriate word. The sentence discusses how online platforms and digital tools allow learners to progress at their own pace and revisit concepts, which indicates personalized learning experiences.

question.en:
Complete the cloze passage by filling in the blanks with the most appropriate words.
Horses___A___companions of humans for thousands of years. They carried warriors into battles, pulled carts___B___villages, and became symbols of power and grace. Even today, they remain important in sports, farming, and therapy sessions. Have you ever wondered why horses are often described as noble animals? Their strength, loyalty, and ability to understand human emotions make them unique. A horse does not simply run; it runs with a spirit that seems___C___(untamed) and free. Take care of your horse well, for it___D___on you for food, shelter, and affection. Groom it regularly and ensure it is treated with kindness. When horses are cared for, they respond with trust and gentleness, creating a bond that lasts a lifetime. How___E___(incredible) it is to watch a herd of horses galloping across an open field! Their hooves thunder against the ground, their manes fly in the wind, and their eyes shine with energy. Truly, horses are living poetry in motion! As the saying goes, "The wind of heaven is that which blows between a horse's ears." Horses remind us that freedom, loyalty, and beauty can exist together in one magnificent creature. They are not just animals of burden but teachers of patience, courage, and respect.


Choose the correct option to fill in the blank (A). [GD Constable, 04 May 2026, Shift 1]

Their hooves thunder against the ground, their manes fly in the wind, and their eyes shine with energy. Truly, horses are living poetry in motion! As the saying goes, "The wind of heaven is that which blows between a horse's ears." Horses remind us that freedom, loyalty, and beauty can exist together in one magnificent creature. They are not just animals of burden but teachers of patience, courage, and respect.


Choose the correct option to fill in the blank (A). [GD Constable, 04 May 2026, Shift 1]

solution.en:
**Rule: The present perfect tense is used to describe an action that started in the past and continues to the present.**
The sentence “Horses ___ companions of humans for thousands of years” describes a state that began thousands of years ago and continues to the present day. The present perfect tense “have been” is used for this purpose.
“was” is past singular.
“had” is past perfect, implying a completed action before another past action.
“will be” is future.
Correct Answer is **have been** because it correctly describes an action that started in the past and continues to the present.
**Ans: have been**

Fill in blank (B) with correct preposition. [GD Constable, 04 May 2026, Shift 1]

solution.en:
**Rule: The preposition “across” is used to indicate movement from one side to the other, or from one place to another.**
The phrase “pulled carts ___ villages” implies they were pulling carts from one village to another or through the countryside between villages. “Across” is the most suitable preposition to indicate movement through or over an area.
“Behind” would mean at the back of villages.
“Into” would mean entering the villages.
“Onto” would mean to the top of villages.
Correct Answer is **across** because it indicates movement through or from one village to another, which fits the context of them pulling carts.
**Ans: across**

question.en:
Complete the cloze passage by filling in the blanks with the most appropriate words.
Last winter, Ananya traveled alone to Shimla for a school competition. The town, covered in snow, looked like a painting that had come alive. She checked into the guesthouse _________ A _________ eager to rehearse her debate speech. But just as she reached for her notes, she realized something alarming, her suitcase _________ B _________ , and the key was missing. Had she dropped it at the railway station? Or had she left it in the train itself? The more she thought, the more restless she became. "Stay calm, Ananya," she whispered to _________ C _________ , "panic will solve nothing." Determined to find a way, she asked the receptionist for help. He suggested calling a locksmith. While waiting, she kept _________ D _________ (pacing) the hall, her mind filled with worry. How embarrassing it would be if she could not present her speech tomorrow! When the locksmith finally arrived, he _________ E _________ (examined) the lock and said confidently, "Do not worry, miss, this will open soon." Within minutes, the suitcase clicked open. What a moment of relief it was! Ananya almost cried with gratitude. That night, while reviewing her speech, she reflected: "Life often tests us with unexpected problems. If we stay calm, solutions eventually appear." She promised herself she would remember this lesson in every challenge ahead.


Fill in blank (A) with the most suitable adverb. [GD Constable, 04 May 2026, Shift 3]

Many people spend hours scrolling through feeds, sometimes feeling isolated or (3)_____ by others' posts. It's important to use social media (4)_____ and take breaks when needed. Setting limits can help maintain a healthy (5)_____ between online and offline life.


(5) [GD Constable, 26 May 2026, Shift 1]

solution.en:
For blank (5), the final sentence talks about maintaining a state between online and offline life. "Routine" (दिनचर्या), "boundary" (सीमा), and "contrast" (अंतर) are not as fitting. The word "balance" (संतुलन) is the most appropriate term to describe a healthy state between two different aspects of life, implying an equal and healthy distribution of time and attention.
Correct Answer is **balance** because it is the most appropriate word to describe a healthy relationship between online and offline life.
**Ans: balance**

One of the main (3)____ of e-books is their convenience; thousands of titles can be stored on a single device. However, some readers still prefer the (4)____ experience of holding a printed book. Despite this, the growth of digital reading is unlikely to (5)____ anytime soon.


(3) [GD Constable, 27 May 2026, Shift 2]

solution.en:
The sentence states that one of the main points of e-books is their convenience. "Advantages" (लाभ) is the correct noun. "Problems" (समस्याएँ), "solutions" (समाधान), and "drawbacks" (कमियाँ) are not the logical choice for a positive feature like convenience.
Correct Answer is **advantages** because convenience is a benefit or an advantage.
**Ans: advantages**

question.en:
Complete the cloze passage by filling in the blanks with the most appropriate words.
It was a rainy evening when Rohan ______A______ a crowded city bus. He had just finished his tuition classes and was eager to reach home. As he searched for his ticket, he ______B______ realized his wallet was missing. His heart began to race. Had he dropped it, or had someone stolen it? “Don’t panic, think carefully,” he told himself. He remembered using the wallet ______C______ a small tea stall near the bus stop. Could it still be there? What if someone else had already picked it up? When the bus stopped at the next signal, Rohan quickly got down. “Please hurry, I must go back!” he whispered under his breath. He ran in the rain, splashing through puddles, his mind full of fear and hope. To his surprise, the tea vendor smiled and said, “Young man, you left this behind.” He held out the wet but safe wallet. What a ______D______ (relief) it was! Rohan almost shouted with joy. He thanked the vendor again and again. This small ______E______ (incident) taught Rohan a big lesson. He realized that not everyone in the world is dishonest, and kindness often appears when least expected. As he walked home in the rain, he thought, “I will never be careless with my belongings again!”


Fill in the blank (A) with the correct verb form. [GD Constable, 28 Apr 2026, Shift 2]

question.hi:

Good communication and respect are essential to build (3)____ among team members. Leaders should encourage cooperation and ensure that everyone feels (4)____. When team members trust and listen to each other, productivity and job satisfaction usually (5)____.


(1) [GD Constable, 29 May 2026, Shift 2]

solution.en:
The correct answer is **'habit'**.

**Key Points:**
• The passage discusses the importance of **teamwork** and positive interactions within a workplace environment.
• The sentence refers to the ability to work well in a team as a 'valuable' attribute.
• **'Habit'** refers to a settled or regular tendency or practice. In a professional context, being a team player is often seen as a consistent **behavioral habit** that contributes to a healthy and productive atmosphere.
• While other terms like 'skill' or 'strength' are often used, **'habit'** emphasizes the repetitive and consistent nature of cooperative behavior in the workplace.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

**Additional Information:**
• **Strength:** Refers to a particular quality or feature that gives someone an advantage.
• **Tool:** Usually refers to a physical object or a specific method/software used to perform a task.
• **Skill:** Refers to the expertise or ability to do something well, typically acquired through training.
solution.hi:
सही उत्तर **'habit'** है।

**मुख्य बिंदु (Key Points):**
• गद्यांश कार्यस्थल के माहौल में **टीम वर्क (teamwork)** और सकारात्मक बातचीत के महत्व पर चर्चा करता है।
• वाक्य में एक टीम में अच्छी तरह से काम करने की क्षमता को एक 'कीमती' गुण के रूप में संदर्भित किया गया है।
• **'Habit' (आदत)** का अर्थ एक स्थापित या नियमित प्रवृत्ति या अभ्यास है। पेशेवर संदर्भ में, एक टीम प्लेयर होना अक्सर एक सुसंगत **व्यवहारिक आदत** के रूप में देखा जाता है जो एक स्वस्थ और उत्पादक माहौल में योगदान देता है।
• यद्यपि 'skill' या 'strength' जैसे अन्य शब्दों का अक्सर उपयोग किया जाता है, लेकिन **'habit'** कार्यस्थल में सहयोगात्मक व्यवहार की दोहरावदार और सुसंगत प्रकृति पर जोर देता है।

इसलिए, सही उत्तर **Option 4** है।

**अतिरिक्त जानकारी (Additional Information):**
• **Strength:** किसी विशिष्ट गुण या विशेषता को संदर्भित करता है जो किसी को लाभ पहुंचाता है।
• **Tool:** आमतौर पर किसी कार्य को करने के लिए उपयोग की जाने वाली भौतिक वस्तु या विशिष्ट विधि/सॉफ्टवेयर को संदर्भित करता है।
• **Skill:** किसी कार्य को अच्छी तरह से करने की विशेषज्ञता या क्षमता को संदर्भित करता है, जो आमतौर पर प्रशिक्षण के माध्यम से प्राप्त की जाती है।

India, as a nation ____ A ____ a rich cultural, scientific, and historical legacy, confers several prestigious awards to honour extraordinary achievements and contributions across different fields. Among these, the highest-ranking awards ____ B ____ special significance, as they represent the nation's deepest gratitude and recognition of excellence. At the pinnacle of civilian honours stands the Bharat Ratna, instituted in 1954. It is the highest civilian award of India, awarded for exceptional service in art, literature, science, and public service of the highest order. Over the years, eminent personalities like Dr. B. R. Ambedkar, Lata Mangeshkar, and Sachin Tendulkar have been recipients of this rare honour. In the realm of ____ C ____ (gallantry), the Param Vir Chakra (PVC) is the nation's most distinguished military award. It is presented for acts of ____ D ____ (conspicuous) bravery and supreme sacrifice in the presence of the enemy. Brave soldiers like Major Somnath Sharma and Captain Vikram Batra have been decorated with this honour, symbolizing courage and patriotism at its peak. In addition, India also recognizes valour through other gallantry awards like the Ashoka Chakra, the highest peacetime bravery award. For contributions in civilian life, the Padma Awards, Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan, and Padma Shri acknowledge distinguished service in varied disciplines. These awards not only celebrate individual achievements but also ____ E ____ generations by highlighting the values of dedication, courage, and service to the nation. They embody India's respect for those who go beyond personal ambition to contribute to society and the country's progress.


Fill in blank (B) with the most appropriate verb form. [GD Constable, 30 Apr 2026, Shift 1]

solution.en:
**Rule: The subject 'awards' is plural, so the verb must be plural.**
The subject for blank B is "awards." Since "awards" is a plural noun, the verb that follows must be plural to agree with it. In the simple present tense, the plural form is "hold."
holds — singular form, used with a singular subject like "he," "she," or "it."
holding — present participle, requires a helping verb like "are."
holed — past tense of "hole," meaning to make a hole in; irrelevant here.
Correct Answer is **hold** because the plural subject "awards" requires the plural verb form "hold."
**Ans: hold**

solution.en:

Intelligence in planning — related to mental ability, not physical bravery.

Correct Answer is **Courage and heroic bravery** because the passage defines gallantry in the context of military awards as acts of conspicuous bravery and sacrifice.
**Ans: Courage and heroic bravery**

solution.en:

Hidden (छिपा हुआ) — antonym, meaning kept out of sight.
Insignificant (मामूली) — too small or unimportant to be worth consideration; unrelated.
Ordinary (सामान्य) — with no special or distinctive features; unrelated.
Correct Answer is **Noticeable** because it is the closest synonym to "conspicuous," which means easily seen or noticed.
**Ans: Noticeable**

question.en:
Complete the cloze passage by filling in the blanks with the most appropriate words.

Cartoons and fantasy shows have become an inseparable part of childhood. Children today spend hours watching animated characters who fight villains, explore magical lands, or solve mysteries. While such content ________ A ________ entertainment and imagination, it also shapes the way children think and behave. Psychologists point out that children often imitate what they see. A child who watches violent cartoons may become aggressive, while one who watches educational programs ________ B ________ develop problem-solving skills. Thus, the impact is not always negative, but it depends on the type of content consumed. Fantasy worlds encourage creativity, but they can also create unrealistic expectations. If children live too much in imaginary lands, they will struggle to deal ________ C ________ real-life challenges. For example, believing that problems disappear magically can prevent them from building resilience. Parents, therefore, play a key role. They should guide children toward shows that are age-appropriate and discuss with them the difference between fiction and reality. A balanced approach is necessary, because neither complete ________ D ________ (restriction) nor unlimited freedom is healthy. As one expert said, "Cartoons are like fire: they can warm if used wisely or burn if left unchecked." This metaphor ________ E ________ (illustrates) the double-edged nature of media influence on young minds.


Choose the correct form of the verb to fill in blank (A). [GD Constable, 30 Apr 2026, Shift 2]

Actions (कार्रवाई) — aligns with deontological ethics, which focuses on the morality of actions themselves.

Fallacies (विसंगति) — errors in reasoning; incorrect.
Correct Answer is **actions** because deontological ethics is primarily concerned with the morality of actions.

solution.en:
Consequentialism judges the morality of an action based on its results. The "net outcomes" implies a balancing of good and bad results, which is central to this ethical theory.
Goods — implies only positive values; not a complete representation.
Outcomes — the correct term for the results of an action.
Benefits — one-sided; ignores potential harms.
Profit — a financial term, too narrow for ethical assessment.
Correct Answer is **outcomes** because consequentialism evaluates actions by their results.
**Ans: outcomes**

Furthermore, scaling up the number of qubits requires (4) ________ control electronics that themselves introduce noise. What should come in the place of blank 1? [Steno, 06 Aug 2025, Shift 1]

solution.en:
Qubit coherence is a major challenge in quantum computing because it is short-lived. "Ephemeral" means lasting for a very short time, which accurately describes the difficulty of maintaining qubit states.
To durable — grammatically incorrect and contextually irrelevant.
Ephemeral — short-lived; matches the problem of qubit coherence.
Permanent — long-lasting; opposite of the problem.
Perennial — enduring; opposite of what is needed.
Correct Answer is **ephemeral** because qubit coherence is a fleeting and unstable state.
**Ans: ephemeral**

The truth of the self-conscious individual lies not in its immediate certainty, but in the dialectical movement of its becoming. Consciousness, in its pursuit of knowledge, initially assumes that its object is something external and independent. Yet, through the labour of experience, it discovers that this object is not truly separate but _________ (1) by consciousness itself.
The apparent duality of subject and object is thus sublated in the dialectic, revealing that knowledge is not the passive reception of a external truth but an active process in which consciousness shapes and ______ (2) its own reality.
This movement unfolds through a series of contradictions, in which each stage of consciousness, believing itself to have attained certainty, encounters its own inadequacy. The master-slave dialectic exemplifies this: self-consciousness seeks recognition from another, yet in asserting its dominance over the other, it paradoxically ______ (3) its own freedom.
The master, in reducing the slave to a mere instrument, deprives himself of a fully realized recognition. Meanwhile, the slave, through labour and self-transformation, attains a deeper awareness of autonomy, demonstrating that freedom is not given but achieve through negation and _______ (4).Spirit (Geist) emerges as the reconciliation of these conflicts-not a static substance but a dynamic process of self-realization. Spirit unfolds historically, manifesting itself _____ (5) in institutions, culture, and philosophy, gradually moving toward absolute knowing. This historical progression is not linear but dialectical, driven by the negation of old forms and the emergence of new ones.


Use the appropriate for of the verb to complete the sentence. (1) [Steno, 06 Aug 2025, Shift 2]

solution.en:
**Rule: Past participle forms are used in passive structures.**
The sentence structure "is not truly separate but _________ (1) by consciousness itself" requires a past participle. "Mediated" is the correct past participle form, indicating that consciousness acts upon the object.
The other options are either present participles, present tense forms, or not in the correct grammatical form.
Correct Answer is **Mediated** because the sentence requires a past participle to complete the passive construction.
**Ans: Mediated**

**Rule: Pronouns that refer back to the subject are reflexive pronouns.**
The pronoun "itself" in "it discovers that this object... by consciousness itself" refers back to the subject "consciousness." Reflexive pronouns are used when the subject and object of a verb are the same.

Read the following passage and answer the questions based on the passage:
While education and wisdom are often conflated in colloquial discourse, a discerning mind perceives a fundamental divergence between the two. Education is the formal acquisition of knowledge, often measured through degrees, academic accolades, and proficiency in structured disciplines. It is delivered through systematic curricula, institutionalized assessment, and theoretical frameworks. However, wisdom transcends this rigidity; it is the judicious application of knowledge to real-life contexts, enriched by experience, introspection, and emotional intelligence. An individual may be extensively educated yet remain bereft of wisdom if they lack the discernment to apply their learning ethically and effectively. Conversely, many wise individuals—farmers, artisans, elders—may not possess formal education, but their decisions exhibit prudence and sagacity cultivated through lived realities. Thus, education equips the mind, but wisdom enriches the soul. In an era dominated by information overload and algorithmic thinking, the schism between the two has widened. Educational institutions often prioritize rote memorization and standardized testing over critical thinking and moral reasoning. Consequently, society produces individuals proficient in problem-solving but deficient in decision-making that requires empathy, patience, or foresight. Wisdom, being innately human, cannot be downloaded or fast-tracked; it is earned through trial, failure, reflection, and a nuanced understanding of human nature. Furthermore, while education is temporally bounded—ending with formal schooling or academic milestones—wisdom is a lifelong pursuit. It does not boast certificates but manifests in humility, ethical consistency, and the ability to navigate ambiguity with grace. Ultimately, the highest form of intelligence lies not merely in knowing what is right, but in consistently choosing to do it, especially when it is inconvenient.


According to the passage, how is wisdom primarily acquired? [CGL, 12 Sep 2025, Shift 1]

solution.en:
The passage says wisdom (प्रज्ञा) is earned through trial, failure, reflection (चिंतन) and lived experience, not through formal schooling.
Through textbooks = education (शिक्षा), not wisdom
Through emotional detachment = opposite of the emotional intelligence described
Through algorithmic thinking = criticised as widening the gap
Correct Answer is **Through experience and reflection** because the author states that wisdom is acquired through experience (अनुभव) and reflection, not formal instruction.
**Ans: Through experience and reflection**

Read the following passage and answer the questions based on the passage :
The proliferation of social media has fundamentally transformed the democratic landscape, acting both as a catalyst for civic engagement and a conduit for manipulation. Platforms like Twitter, Facebook, and Instagram, once relegated to the domain of personal expression, now serve as powerful instruments of political discourse, enabling citizens to articulate opinions, mobilize for causes, and scrutinize authority in real-time. At its core, democracy thrives on the free flow of information, and social media ostensibly democratizes this process by dismantling traditional gatekeeping. Political leaders communicate directly with constituents, bypassing editorial filters, while grassroots movements harness virality to amplify marginalized voices. During critical events—be it elections, protests, or legislative debates—social media acts as a digital agora, fostering participatory dialogue that was once confined to town halls or print columns. However, this unprecedented openness is double-edged. The same platforms that disseminate truth can also propagate misinformation, polarize public opinion, and algorithmically reinforce ideological silos. Electoral interference through fake accounts, coordinated trolling, and the spread of disinformation campaigns have threatened electoral integrity in several democracies. Moreover, emotionally charged content, optimized for engagement rather than accuracy, often eclipses nuanced debate, reducing political discourse to a cacophony of outrage. The role of social media in democracy, therefore, is contingent not just on its technological architecture, but on the ethical frameworks governing its use. Regulatory oversight, media literacy, and algorithmic transparency are essential to harness its democratic potential while mitigating its subversive tendencies. In essence, social media is neither inherently virtuous nor inherently corrosive—it is a mirror of societal intent. Whether it becomes a pillar of democratic resilience or a tool of populist distortion depends largely on how it is wielded by citizens, institutions, and platforms alike


<p>What primary democratic function does social media serve, as per the paragraph?</p> [CGL, 12 Sep 2025, Shift 2]

Promoting entertainment — not the democratic function
Replacing newspapers — not claimed
Organizing trade unions — not the point
Correct Answer is **Facilitating free flow of information** because that is the primary democratic role assigned to social media in the passage.
**Ans: Facilitating free flow of information**

question.en:
Read the following passage and answer the questions based on the passage :
Group thinking, often referred to as groupthink, is a psychological phenomenon wherein the desire for unanimity within a group overrides the motivation to appraise alternative viewpoints critically. It frequently leads to flawed decision-making because dissent is either internally suppressed or socially penalized. Social conformity, its close ally, describes the act of aligning one's beliefs or behaviours with those of a majority, often subconsciously, in pursuit of acceptance or avoidance of conflict. In tightly knit groups—such as corporate boards, political committees, or academic panels—individual members may refrain from expressing contrarian ideas, fearing ostracization or reputational risk. Over time, this collective homogeneity breeds intellectual stagnation, reducing innovation and enhancing vulnerability to strategic errors. The infamous Bay of Pigs invasion and the Challenger space shuttle disaster are frequently cited as textbook examples of decisions marred by groupthink. Psychologically, the roots of group conformity lie in our evolutionary inclination toward tribal belonging, where deviation was historically associated with survival risk. In modern society, the same instinct manifests through peer pressure, organizational culture, and digital echo chambers. Algorithms reinforce conformity by curating information bubbles that validate existing biases while filtering out divergent thought. However, the remedy to such cognitive myopia lies in institutionalizing dissent. Constructive disagreement, when encouraged within teams or communities, acts as an intellectual safeguard against tunnel vision. Promoting a culture where counterarguments are respected rather than reprimanded can lead to more robust, balanced, and resilient decision-making. In an age dominated by viral trends, polarized discourse, and performative alignment, the courage to question consensus is both rare and essential. True progress emerges not from blind allegiance to majority norms, but from critical inquiry and the audacity to challenge the comfortable. 


<p>What is the central idea of groupthink as discussed in the passage?</p> [CGL, 12 Sep 2025, Shift 3]

solution.en:
Groupthink (समूह-चिंतन) is defined as the desire for unanimity (सर्वसम्मति) overpowering realistic critique.
Collaborative brainstorming — positive teamwork, not groupthink
Trusting only experts / promoting decentralization — not the central idea
Correct Answer is **Valuing consensus over critique** because groupthink means preferring consensus (सहमति) to critical evaluation.
**Ans: Valuing consensus over critique**

Read the following passage and answer the questions based on the passage:
For seventeen-year-old Meera, adolescence was not merely a phase of hormonal transitions and academic aspirations—it became an arena where perception and self-worth collided with insidious intensity. In a world saturated with curated digital aesthetics and algorithm-driven beauty hierarchies, Meera’s own reflection began to feel less like truth and more like betrayal. Every scroll through her social media feed deepened a gnawing dissonance: between her authentic self and the impossible silhouettes idolized online. This wasn’t mere teenage insecurity—it manifested as a systematic devaluation of her physical self. Gradually, she adopted punitive behaviors: food became conditional, mirrors became adversaries, and compliments transformed into cryptic reminders of inadequacy. The subtle descent into dysmorphia was neither loud nor linear. Academically capable and socially pleasant, Meera wore the mask of normalcy with precision. Yet beneath the practiced smiles was a quiet implosion. She began withdrawing emotionally, rationalizing her distress as vanity, and trivializing her worth. The turning point came not with drama, but with silence—a refusal to eat for days, which led to medical intervention. Therapeutic engagement introduced her to the concept of self-image distortion, and the emotional scaffolding required to rebuild her fractured sense of identity. Through sustained counseling, Meera disentangled societal impositions from intrinsic value. She began to internalize that beauty is not a monolith dictated by culture but a spectrum shaped by diversity, health, and self-compassion. Meera’s narrative is not a singular anomaly but a mirror to a larger epidemic— where teenagers battle unspoken wars behind flawless digital façades. Combating this requires more than awareness; it calls for critical media literacy, empathetic environments, and systemic redefinition of beauty norms that extend beyond superficial metrics.


<p>What does the phrase "gnawing dissonance" in the passage most likely refer to?</p> [CGL, 13 Sep 2025, Shift 1]

1.en: Her hunger due to skipped meals

2.en: Conflict between her inner worth and online ideals

solution.en:
“Gnawing dissonance” (कुतरती असंगति) is the clash between Meera’s authentic self-worth and the impossible online beauty ideals.
Hunger from skipped meals — too literal
Disagreement with teachers / detachment from academics — not the phrase’s target
Correct Answer is **Conflict between her inner worth and online ideals** because that is the dissonance (अंतर-द्वंद्व) the passage describes.
**Ans: Conflict between her inner worth and online ideals**

In contemporary discourse, the debate between entrepreneurship and conventional employment has gained remarkable traction. While traditional employment offers predictability, structured growth, and a defined career trajectory, entrepreneurship appeals to those seeking autonomy, innovation, and the potential for exponential returns. However, both paths are fraught with distinct advantages and inherent uncertainties. Employment, particularly within established organizations, provides financial stability, social recognition, and institutional support. Employees are not burdened with existential risks such as capital loss or market unpredictability. Instead, they operate within frameworks of responsibility and hierarchy, where risk is absorbed at higher managerial levels. For many, this structure offers psychological comfort and a clear roadmap for progression. Conversely, entrepreneurship demands resilience, resourcefulness, and a high tolerance for ambiguity. Entrepreneurs must navigate volatile markets, regulatory complexities, and the absence of assured income—challenges often underestimated by aspirants. Yet, for those with a risk appetite and creative acumen, entrepreneurship promises a unique form of fulfillment. It allows individuals to disrupt existing paradigms, build ventures from the ground up, and possibly shape industries. Societal perceptions further complicate the dichotomy. In many cultures, steady employment is seen as the hallmark of success, while entrepreneurial endeavors are often perceived as reckless or unstable—until they succeed. This perception, however, is gradually shifting as global startup ecosystems mature and innovation becomes synonymous with progress. The real decision, therefore, lies not in which path is superior but in aligning one's temperament, values, and long-term goals with the demands of each route. Entrepreneurship may offer liberation, but it is not without sacrifice. Employment may provide security, but it can come at the cost of creative constraint. A reflective, context-aware approach—not blind aspiration—is essential for navigating this professional crossroads. 


<p>According to the passage, which quality is most crucial for entrepreneurs?</p> [CGL, 13 Sep 2025, Shift 2]

solution.en:
The passage treats resilience (लचीलापन / पुनर्स्थापन क्षमता) as the quality an entrepreneur most needs amid risk and uncertainty.
Obedience / conformity = employment traits
Delegation = useful but not named as the crucial quality
Correct Answer is **Resilience** because the author presents resilience as essential to surviving entrepreneurial risk.
**Ans: Resilience**
